nuances.statement: Listed at high exposure and kept, because the rule for dropping a profession is technological obsolescence of the NEED, not of the current method. People still want drawn worlds, comics and picture books. What has collapsed is the price of a single competent image.

The employed figures describe a staff concept artist at a game or animation studio. A freelance illustrator's income is lumpy and commission-driven, and the range understates both its floor and its ceiling.

professions.one_liner: Decides what a game is and how it plays - rules, levels, difficulty, economy and story.

deviating_roles.why: Narrative design is writing - branching dialogue, world lore and character. It shares almost nothing with tuning a difficulty curve or an in-game economy.
Economy and balance work is applied statistics on player behaviour data. It is the quantitative end of a profession most people join for the creative end.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree. Game design programmes exist but studios hire on shipped work.
Two or three finished small games, or levels and mods built in Unity or Unreal. Finished beats ambitious.
Junior designer or QA-to-design at a studio; India's studios cluster in Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad and Mumbai.

entrance_exams.note: None. Entry is on shipped work.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Independent release on Steam, itch.io or the app stores, usually as a two-to-five person team. Realistic only after several years of shipped experience.

ai_exposure.reason: A clarity-heavy profession, which is what protects it. Environment Artist and Character Artist (Games) are exposed - they are asset production and generative tools reach them directly. Game Designer, Level Designer and Systems & Economy Designer are protected: the work is deciding what would be fun for a specific audience and then being proved wrong in playtesting, which is a judgment loop rather than an output task.

nuances.statement: Distinct from Sector 1's Game & Interactive Media Developer, and the substitution test is what separates them. Remove the game from the developer and a software engineer remains; remove it from the designer and nothing does. One writes the engine, the other decides what the engine should make you feel.

Moderate, not high. India has a very large games MARKET and a much smaller game DEVELOPMENT industry - most Indian studios do art and engineering services for foreign titles rather than original design. Reading market size as the number of design jobs is the error DECISIONS.md 8.45 warns against.

professions.one_liner: Plans the inside of homes, shops and offices - layout, light, materials and furniture.

deviating_roles.why: Lighting design is photometrics and electrical layout as much as aesthetics, and is usually done for other designers rather than for the client directly.
Coordination is site work - chasing carpenters, contractors and delivery dates. It is where most interior projects are actually won or lost, and it involves no design.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
B.Des or B.Sc in Interior Design (4 years), or a 1-2 year diploma. Neither is legally required to practise.
Two to three years with a firm, learning execution - materials, vendors, costing and site supervision.
Designer at a studio or design-and-build firm, or independent practice.

entrance_exams.note: Neither is required and most practising interior designers sat neither. Private colleges admit on marks or their own test.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Independent practice, usually as a design-and-build studio taking a margin on execution as well as a design fee. This is the normal shape of the profession in India, not an exception.

ai_exposure.reason: Layout options and renders generate easily, and Interior Stylist and Space Planner feel that first. What does not automate is the middle of the job: standing on a site where the wall is 40mm out, the client has changed their mind and the carpenter has cut the wrong sheet. Interior Project Coordinator and Fixture & Joinery Designer are protected by that reality.

nuances.statement: Null, and this is the sector's most consequential settled fact. The Architects Act 1972 protects the TITLE 'architect' - it does not protect the ACTIVITY of designing interiors. Anyone in India may design and execute an interior with no registration and no degree. The Institute of Indian Interior Designers is a voluntary professional association, not a statutory regulator.

The employed range describes a designer on a firm's payroll. Independent practice earns on execution margin rather than fee, and that is where the real income in this profession sits - which is exactly what mid_career_lpa excludes by design.

professions.one_liner: Designs clothing and textiles - from mass-market ranges to couture and costume.

deviating_roles.why: Surface design is repeat geometry, colourways and material behaviour, done at a desk. It never involves dressing a person or presenting a collection.
Styling is selection and persuasion for a shoot, a client or a film - the stylist designs nothing and makes nothing, but decides what reads.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
NIFT Entrance Examination, NID DAT or UCEED. Private and state colleges admit on their own tests.
B.Des in Fashion Design (4 years) at NIFT, NID or a private institute.
Assistant designer at an export house, a domestic brand or a designer studio.

entrance_exams.note: NIFT is the volume route - 17,974 candidates for roughly 4,837 seats. It is a statutory institute under the NIFT Act 2006 and grants its own degrees.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Own label, a boutique, or freelance design for export houses. In India this is the normal route to a real income in this profession rather than an alternative to it.

ai_exposure.reason: Print & Pattern Designer and Fashion Illustrator are the exposed roles - generating colourways and repeats is exactly what image models do well. The rest of the profession is protected by cloth: fit, drape, fabric behaviour and how a garment moves on a body are physical problems learned by making, and a design that cannot be sewn at a price is not a design. Costume Designer is protected further by having to serve a character and a director.

nuances.statement: The employed range describes an assistant or in-house designer at an export house or brand - where most NIFT graduates go, and it pays modestly. The public image of the profession comes from the very small number who run a successful label, and that income is entrepreneurship, excluded from mid_career_lpa by design.

NIFT at 3.7 applicants per seat is the MOST OPEN national design gate in the registry - 17 times easier to enter than UCEED. Fashion is widely believed to be a hard course to get into; at NIFT's scale, it is not.

professions.one_liner: Turns a design into something a factory can actually sew - patterns, fit, samples, quality.

deviating_roles.why: Merchandising is buyer correspondence, costing and delivery schedules. Pattern making next to it is three-dimensional geometry done on paper and cloth.
Flattening a three-dimensional body into two-dimensional pieces, then grading it across eight sizes, is the most technical skill in the apparel chain and is done almost entirely alone.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream. Physics, Chemistry and Maths are needed ONLY for the NIFT B.F.Tech degree route, not for the trade route.
A 1-2 year diploma in apparel manufacturing or pattern making - NIFT, ATDC or an NSQF-aligned course.
Sampling or production floor at an export house in Tiruppur, Noida, Bengaluru or Ludhiana.
Move into pattern making, fit or quality - the skills that survive when a line is automated.

entrance_exams.note: Required only for the NIFT B.F.Tech degree. The diploma and trade routes into this profession have no entrance exam at all.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: An independent sampling or pattern-making unit serving several export houses - a common step once a pattern master has a reputation in a cluster.

ai_exposure.reason: Protected by cloth and by the factory floor. CAD Pattern & Grading Specialist is the most exposed role, since grading is rule-based and already largely automated in software. Fit Technician and Pattern Maker are the safest work in the apparel chain: judging why a sleeve pulls on a real body, and knowing what to change, is a physical skill built over years.

nuances.statement: 'any' is correct for the profession but hides a real fork. The NIFT B.F.Tech degree route requires Physics, Chemistry and Maths in class 12; the diploma and trade routes require nothing. A student without PCM is shut out of that one degree, not out of this profession.

Deliberately named around PATTERN and FIT rather than around factory management. Generic production planning and line balancing survive the substitution test - they are the same job in an electronics plant - and belong in Sector 2. Pattern making, grading and fit do not survive it: they exist only because cloth behaves as it does.

professions.one_liner: Cuts and sews clothing to measure or to a pattern - the base of the whole apparel industry.

deviating_roles.why: Factory line sewing is one operation repeated to a standard and a piece rate, with no customer contact at all. A boutique tailor's day is largely reading a customer, managing expectations and being trusted with a wedding.
Cutting from measurements with no paper pattern is the high skill of the trade, held by relatively few people and learned over a decade at a bench.

path_to_entry.requirement: None. Many enter after class 8 or 10.
Apprenticeship with a working tailor, an ITI Sewing Technology trade, or an NSQF short course.
Operator at a garment unit, or with a neighbourhood tailor.
Own shop with one to three machines, which is where the income actually changes.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Own tailoring shop or boutique, taking measure-to-order work and alterations directly. Capital needed is one or two machines.

ai_exposure.reason: Almost untouchable. Sewing a garment to fit a specific person is physical work in an unstructured environment, and every attempt to automate garment assembly has foundered on the fact that cloth is limp and will not hold its shape. Sewing Machine Operator is the only role with real exposure, and that is to automation of the factory line rather than to AI.

nuances.statement: These are EMPLOYED figures, largely piece-rate work in garment units, and they sit close to the legal minimum wage. They are not what a tailor with an established shop earns, and the record has no sourced figure for that - which is what the admin_review is for.

High and stable, and worth stating plainly because the trade looks old-fashioned. Indian clothing is still overwhelmingly stitched to measure or altered after purchase, and both are jobs nobody has found a way to do remotely.

admin_review.reason: No sourced figure exists for what an independent tailor or boutique owner earns. Without it the record shows 3.0 LPA and reads as a dead end, when independence is the normal path in this trade and the reason people enter it. This is the same gap flagged on Mason in Sector 2 and needs the same fix: a sourced self_employment.ceiling_lpa.

professions.one_liner: Weaves cloth by hand on a loom - saris, stoles and yardage, mostly at home.

deviating_roles.why: The coordinator's day is government schemes, buyer orders, cooperative paperwork and getting yarn to twenty households. It touches the loom only indirectly.
Setting up a jacquard and punching design cards is mechanical problem-solving. It is the engineering role inside a craft trade, and it serves a whole cluster.

path_to_entry.requirement: None. The trade is usually learned at home from a parent, starting in the early teens.
Family apprenticeship, or a Weavers' Service Centre or Indian Institute of Handloom Technology course.
Weaving on piece rate for a master weaver or a cooperative society.
Own loom, selling through a cooperative, a state emporium or direct online sale.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Weaving on your own loom and selling direct - through a cooperative, a state emporium, a design label or online - instead of on piece rate for a master weaver. Direct sale is the single biggest determinant of a weaver's income.

ai_exposure.reason: The lowest AI exposure in this sector and among the lowest in the dataset. Handloom weaving is defined by being done by hand; the moment it is automated it becomes powerloom cloth, a different product in a different market. The threat to this profession has never been software - it is powerloom competition and the price of yarn.

nuances.statement: The only economics block in this sector with a government source behind it, and it is a subsistence one: the Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20 found 67.1 percent of weavers earning under Rs 5,000 a month and only 6.7 percent above Rs 10,000. The range shown is that distribution converted to lakh per year.

26.7 lakh weavers and 8.5 lakh allied workers is a very large headcount, and reading it as opportunity would be the exact error DECISIONS.md 8.45 warns against. Demand for handloom CLOTH is steady; demand for a weaver's LABOUR is priced at subsistence. Both are true and a student needs to be told both.

Fails the compensation filter at 1.2 LPA, and rightly - but the profession is listed anyway. It is not disappearing, it is where 26.7 lakh people already are, and the application can reverse the filter for a student who is one of them.

admin_review.reason: No sourced figure exists for what a weaver selling DIRECT earns - through a cooperative, an emporium or a design collaboration. That number is the whole difference between the census distribution and a viable livelihood, and without it the record shows only the piece-rate floor.

professions.one_liner: Makes objects by hand as a trade - pottery, woodwork, metalware, cane, embroidery.

path_to_entry.requirement: None. Most craft skills are inherited within a family or a community.
Apprenticeship under a working artisan, or a Guru-Shishya or design development scheme of the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts).
Artisan identity card, which is what opens access to government schemes, exhibitions and credit.
Producing on order for exporters and buyers, or selling direct at melas, emporia and online marketplaces.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Selling your own work directly - at exhibitions and melas, through a state emporium, or on an online marketplace - rather than producing on piece rate for an exporter. An artisan identity card unlocks the scheme and exhibition side of that.

ai_exposure.reason: As close to unexposed as this dataset contains. Every one of these roles is hand skill applied to a physical material in an unstructured setting, and part of the product's value is that a person made it. Where AI touches the trade at all it is on the selling side - listings, photographs and descriptions - not on the making.

nuances.statement: 6.4 million artisans is INDUSTRY SIZE, not profession size, and the distinction matters more here than almost anywhere. The headcount is enormous and shrinking in real terms as younger family members leave; demand for the output is real but concentrated in exports and tourism, both volatile.

Judgment, with no sources, and that is a genuine failure rather than a shrug. No usable earnings survey for Indian handicraft artisans was found. The figures shown are reasoned from the handloom census next door - a related trade with a similar structure - and should not be trusted until sourced.

Narrow despite ten very different materials. A potter and a cane worker look unalike but sit in almost the same psychometric place: hand skill, patience, spatial judgment, tolerance for repetition and an informal income. The material differs; the person the work suits does not.

admin_review.reason: Two gaps, both money. There is no sourced income figure for handicraft artisans at all, and none for what an artisan selling direct earns versus one on piece rate for an exporter. Until both exist this is the least evidenced record in the sector, and it describes 6.4 million people.

professions.one_liner: Designs and makes jewellery - from bench work at the anvil to CAD for a retail chain.

deviating_roles.why: Design here is drawing and 3D modelling for a brand or a retail range, done on a screen. Bench work next to it is fine motor metalwork learned by apprenticeship, and the two rarely sit in the same person.
Gemmology is identification and grading under a loupe against a standard - a laboratory discipline attached to a craft trade.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream, or none for the bench route.
Apprenticeship in a karigar workshop for the bench trade, or a jewellery design diploma or GJSCI-aligned course for the design side.
Karigar unit, a retail chain's design team, or an export manufacturing unit in Mumbai, Surat, Jaipur or Coimbatore.
Own workshop supplying retailers, which is the standard shape of the Indian trade.

entrance_exams.note: None. Both the bench route and the design route are entered without an entrance exam.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Own karigar workshop taking order work from retailers and wholesalers - the dominant structure of Indian jewellery manufacture, which is a network of small independent units rather than factories.

ai_exposure.reason: The bench is safe; the drawing board is not. Goldsmith, Bench Jeweller, Diamond & Gemstone Setter and Polisher & Finisher are hand skills on precious material where a mistake is unrecoverable, and none of that is a text problem. CAD Jewellery Designer is the exposed role - generating ring variations on a theme is exactly what these tools do - and Gemmologist sits in between, since machine grading of stones is already deployed commercially.

nuances.statement: Null. Nothing licenses a goldsmith in India. Hallmarking regulates the PRODUCT and the seller, not the craftsperson, and skill in this trade is certified by apprenticeship and reputation inside a karigar network rather than by any council.

This is a single profession containing two quite different people, kept as one because they share an object of concern and a workshop. A student should read the deviating roles before choosing: the bench route needs no degree and no English; the CAD route needs both.

professions.one_liner: Comes up with the idea behind an ad and writes the words that carry it.

deviating_roles.why: The art director thinks in image and layout while the copywriter thinks in language. Agencies deliberately pair the two as a team for exactly that difference.
Strategy is the argument BEFORE the idea - who the audience is, what they believe now and what would change it. It is analytical work that constrains the creative brief rather than answering it.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree. English, mass communication and design are common but nothing is required.
A spec book - campaigns you invented for real brands. This is what agencies read; the degree is not.
Junior copywriter or junior art director at an agency, or in-house on a brand team.

entrance_exams.note: No exam is required. MICAT is the one well-known private entrance, and it leads to a postgraduate communication degree rather than to the job itself.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance copywriting and independent creative consultancy, often for the same agencies and brands worked with in-house. Very common in this profession after 5-6 years.

ai_exposure.reason: Volume copy is already being generated, and Brand Content Writer, Digital Campaign Creative and Packaging & Retail Copywriter feel it directly - product descriptions, social captions and variant headlines were the industry's junior training ground and are now largely a prompt. Creative Strategist and Art Director (Advertising) are the protected end: deciding what a brand should say, to whom, and defending that to a client who wants something else, is clarity work.

nuances.statement: High, and the shape of the damage matters. This profession trained people by giving juniors the boring copy to write. That rung is going, which means the profession may keep its senior jobs while losing the ladder that produced them.
One of the most open well-paid entries in the dataset. There is no exam, no licence, no required subject and no required degree discipline - a spec book written at home is a complete application.

professions.one_liner: Makes art as the work itself - painting, sculpture, printmaking, murals, installation.

deviating_roles.why: Public art is commissioned, scheduled, physically large and negotiated with a client or a municipality. It is project work with deadlines, unlike studio practice.

These are the paid jobs inside the art world that involve no authorship - fabricating, crating, hanging and caring for other people's work. They are how many artists actually earn while building a practice.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
BFA (4 years) at a government art college or university department. Not legally required, but it is where a practice and a network usually start.
Build a body of work and exhibit - group shows, residencies, art fairs.
Gallery representation and commissions, almost always alongside teaching, design work or studio assisting.

entrance_exams.note: CUET UG is used for BFA admission at central universities; most state art colleges run their own aptitude test. Neither is required to work as an artist.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Selling through galleries, commissions, residencies and direct sale. Practically every practising fine artist is self-employed by definition - the question is what subsidises the practice, and for most it is teaching or design work.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure, for a reason worth stating precisely: what is sold here is not an image, it is an object made by a named person with a body of work behind it. Image generation devalues illustration, which sells the picture; it does not touch a sculpture, a print run or a commissioned mural. Portrait Artist is the most exposed role, and even there the market is largely for a painted object rather than a likeness.

nuances.statement: Low is honest and is not a reason to drop it. India has a small collecting market and few public art budgets, so the number of people who live on art alone is genuinely small. The work exists and is done; it is rarely a whole income.

The range is wide and skewed because the distribution is: a small number of represented artists earn very well and most earn little from art itself. The figures assume a practice subsidised by teaching or design work, which is the normal case.

admin_review.reason: No sourced income data for Indian fine artists was found, and the employed range is unusually speculative even by this sector's standards. The record also has no figure for what gallery representation actually changes, which is the single most important economic fact in this profession.

professions.one_liner: Designs and makes shoes, bags and leather goods - form, fit, materials and the last.

deviating_roles.why: Repair is manual craft learned on the job with no design component, usually self-employed at a roadside stall or a small shop. It is the base layer of this profession and its most accessible entry.
Leather technology is chemistry - tanning, finishing, testing and effluent. It is a laboratory discipline attached to a design and making trade.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
A diploma or B.Des at FDDI or a CLRI-linked institute, or an LSSC-aligned course; or apprenticeship for the repair and making trades.
Design or development team at a footwear manufacturer - Agra, Kanpur, Chennai and Ambur are the clusters.
Last development, fit or components - the parts of the job that cannot easily be moved to a cheaper country.

entrance_exams.note: FDDI's entrance is the main institutional route. FDDI is an Institute of National Importance under the FDDI Act 2017. The trade routes need no exam.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and studio ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: A small made-to-order or repair unit, or a components workshop supplying larger manufacturers. India's footwear industry is built on exactly these small units.

ai_exposure.reason: Protected by fit and by material. A shoe has to be walked in, and the last - the form a shoe is built around - is developed by physical iteration against real feet. Footwear Designer is the most exposed role at the styling end; Last & Pattern Developer, Leather Technologist and Cobbler & Shoe Repair Specialist are barely touched.

nuances.statement: Kept separate from Fashion Designer rather than folded into it as job roles, on the merge test in DECISIONS.md 8.95. The object of concern is shared, but the skill set is not: last making, orthopaedic fit, sole construction and leather chemistry have no counterpart in garment design. The trade has its own Skill Council and its own national institute for the same reason.

Cobbler & Shoe Repair Specialist is deliberately inside this profession rather than left out as too small. It is the trade's genuine base layer, needs almost no capital, and is one of the few entries in this dataset open to someone with no schooling at all.

professions.one_liner: Finds out what happened, checks it, and tells the public - in print, on air or online.

deviating_roles.why: Desk work is checking, tightening and headlining other people's copy against a deadline. It never leaves the building, and it is where accuracy is actually enforced.
Anchoring is live performance under time pressure - reading, listening to a producer and speaking simultaneously. It shares almost nothing with reporting except the subject matter.
Data journalism is analysis and visualisation of records and datasets. The source is a spreadsheet rather than a person, and the skill is closer to a Data Analyst's.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree. A BA or MA in journalism or mass communication is common and is not required - subject expertise in economics, law or science is often worth more.
Published work. Student papers, campus magazines, freelance pieces and a blog all count; editors hire on what you have written.
Trainee reporter or sub-editor at a newspaper, broadcaster or digital newsroom.

entrance_exams.note: None is required. IIMC is the best-known public postgraduate route; most working journalists in India entered without any of these.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance reporting, a subscriber-funded newsletter or an independent digital outlet. Increasingly common in India as staff newsrooms shrink, and it is where much of the serious reporting now happens.

ai_exposure.reason: Aggregation, rewriting agency copy and templated market or sports reports are already automated, and those were the trainee's job. Sub-Editor & Copy Editor and Business Journalist on routine numbers are the exposed roles. What no model can do is be in the room: Correspondent, Photojournalist and any reporting that depends on a source trusting a named person are protected, and Fact-Checker is protected by being the answer to the problem.

nuances.statement: Anchored on the Majithia Wage Board, the only statutory pay schedule in this sector - entry basic of Rs 13,000 a month at the largest newspaper groups down to Rs 7,000 at the smallest, plus 20-35 percent variable pay and allowances. Two caveats travel with it and both matter: those are 2011 figures never since revised, and the Act binds NEWSPAPER establishments only.

Null. The Press Council of India is statutory but regulates newspapers' CONDUCT, not journalists' right to work - it cannot strike anyone off. PIB accreditation is often mistaken for a licence; it only grants access to government premises.

Moderate, and the shape is unusual: print newsrooms are contracting while digital and regional-language news are growing, so total employment is roughly flat with the jobs moving. A student should know that the growing half pays worse and is outside the Working Journalists Act altogether.

professions.one_liner: Writes and edits the words other people publish - websites, manuals, books, documentation.

deviating_roles.why: Both write to a standard rather than a voice - an API reference or a clinical study report is judged on precision and completeness. Medical writing carries regulatory consequence, which is why it pays best in this profession.
Book-length work is a solitary two-year commitment with no salary attached. It is the one role here that is a vocation rather than a job.
Translation is deep two-language competence, and in India usually English plus one Indian language at professional depth. It is a different skill from composition.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream. Technical and medical writing favour a science background but do not require one.
Any bachelor's degree. For Medical Writer a life-sciences, pharmacy or medical degree is effectively expected.
A portfolio of published or sample work. This is the whole application - there is no exam and no certificate anyone checks.
In-house content or documentation team, an agency, a publisher, or a pharmaceutical or CRO writing group.

entrance_exams.note: None. There is no entrance examination into any part of this profession.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance writing and editing, which is how a large share of this work is already bought. Medical and technical writers command the highest independent rates because the domain knowledge is scarce.

ai_exposure.reason: The most exposed profession in this sector and one of the most exposed in the dataset. SEO Content Writer and general Content Writer produce exactly what language models produce, and that market has already repriced. Proofreader is going the same way. What holds is where someone must be ACCOUNTABLE for the text: Medical Writer, where a clinical study report is a regulatory document with a named author, and UX Writer, where the words are a product decision. Book Editor and Commissioning Editor are protected by judgment about what is worth publishing at all.

nuances.statement: Technical Writer and Medical Writer were both promised to this sector from elsewhere - Technical Writer from Software & Computing, Medical Writer from Healthcare. Both are kept as job roles rather than professions because the skill set is the same writing craft applied to a different domain, which is what the merge test in DECISIONS.md 8.95 asks.

High, and the honest framing is that this profession is repricing rather than disappearing. Demand for text has gone up, not down; what has collapsed is the price of ordinary text. The surviving work is the text that carries consequence or requires domain knowledge a model cannot be trusted with unsupervised.

Moderate rather than high, which is a downgrade from where this profession sat two years ago. Content and SEO writing was one of the largest entry-level employers of Indian arts graduates, and that intake has visibly contracted.

professions.one_liner: Decides what a film or series is and gets it made - story, cast, performance, final cut.

deviating_roles.why: Screenwriting is solitary structural work done long before anyone is on set, and many screenwriters never direct. It is the one role here that needs no crew.

The AD department runs the schedule and the continuity - it is logistics under pressure, and it is how almost everyone in Indian film actually enters. Invention is not the job; keeping a hundred people to a call sheet is.
Casting is reading people and remembering hundreds of them. It is a talent-scouting job that happens to sit inside filmmaking.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.

Any bachelor's degree, or a film school - FTII Pune, SRFTI Kolkata, or a private institute. Film school is a strong advantage and is not required; a large share of working Indian directors did not attend one.
Three to six years as an assistant director. This is the real entry route in Indian film and it is poorly paid.
Direct short films, ads or web content, then features. Documentary and advertising are the routes that pay while you build a reel.

entrance_exams.note: Neither is required. FTII and SRFTI share the JET entrance and are extremely competitive, but film school is one route into this profession rather than the route.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Independent and commissioned work - documentaries, advertising films, corporate video and streaming commissions. Almost every Indian director is legally self-employed, hired project to project.

ai_exposure.reason: The most clarity-heavy profession in this sector, which is what protects it. Generative video produces shots; it does not decide what story is worth telling, what a performance should feel like, or whether a scene is working. Ad Film Director is the most exposed role, because short commercial video is where synthetic footage is being adopted fastest. Documentary Filmmaker is the least - it depends on access, trust and being physically present.

nuances.statement: Six years is longer than an MBBS, and it is not spent studying. It is three to six years of assistant directing on very low pay before anyone is trusted with a film. The runway, not the fee, is this profession's real cost of entry.

The range is wide because the distribution is extreme - a working ad-film or streaming director earns well while most people who set out to direct never make a feature. The employed figure describes steady commissioned work, which is what the profession looks like for those who stay in it.

professions.one_liner: Decides how a scene is lit and framed, and operates the camera that records it.

deviating_roles.why: The lighting department is physical trade work - rigging, power, safety and long hours - executing a cinematographer's intent. It is a skilled crew job with a different entry route from the creative one.
The DIT manages colour pipeline, data and on-set monitoring. It is a technical specialism that grew out of digital capture and is closer to post-production.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Film school, a cinematography diploma, or no formal training at all - many enter as camera attendants and learn on set.
Work up through the camera department: attendant, second assistant, focus puller, operator.
Cinematographer on ads, music videos, documentaries or independent films, then longer formats.

entrance_exams.note: Neither is required, and the crew route into this profession involves no exam at all.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance day rates, which is how essentially the whole camera department works. Owning a camera package materially raises what you can charge.

ai_exposure.reason: Protected by being physically present with equipment in a real space. Lighting a face, pulling focus on a moving actor and rigging a crane are not text problems, and no generative tool touches Gaffer, Focus Puller or Steadicam Operator. Digital Imaging Technician is the most exposed role, since colour and data management is increasingly automated software.

nuances.statement: Certificate rather than undergrad, and that is the truth of the camera department: it is a craft entered as an assistant and learned by doing. A degree helps you get the first job and nothing after that.

Marked common because it is nearly universal - the camera department is freelance almost by definition, hired per project at a day rate. There is no meaningful employed version of this profession outside television news and corporate in-house teams.

professions.one_liner: Assembles the shot footage into the film - what stays, what goes, and in what order.

deviating_roles.why: Grading is a visual specialism with its own craft and its own suite. A colourist shapes how a film feels without changing a single cut.
These are accuracy-and-schedule roles rather than storytelling ones, and in India subtitling is a large employer because of the number of languages a release needs.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
An editing diploma or film school, or self-taught on the software - the tools are cheap and the skill is demonstrable.
Cut real footage. A reel of finished work is the entire hiring test.
Assistant editor at a post house, or editing corporate, ad and digital content directly.

entrance_exams.note: Not required. Most editors in India are self-taught or diploma-trained and hired on a reel.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance editing for agencies, production houses and creators - a laptop and a reel are the whole setup, which makes this one of the lowest-capital independent routes in the dataset.

ai_exposure.reason: Split down the middle. Subtitling & Captioning Editor is being automated fastest - machine transcription and translation already do the first pass - and Assistant Editor work like logging, syncing and rough assembly is going the same way. Film Editor proper is protected by the thing the job actually is: deciding what a scene needs, which is judgment about rhythm and performance, argued out with a director over weeks.

nuances.statement: High, and unusually for this sector it is growing rather than flat. Streaming, advertising, corporate video and the creator economy all consume edited video at volume, and India edits a great deal of it for overseas clients as well.

Employed figures describe a post house or in-house team. Freelance editors working directly with agencies and creators can earn considerably more, and the capital needed to start is a laptop - which is why self_employment is marked common.

professions.one_liner: Builds everything you hear that is not music - dialogue, effects, atmosphere, the mix.

deviating_roles.why: Location sound is physical work on set - holding a boom for twelve hours, hearing a problem nobody else notices, and having one chance to capture a take.
Foley is performance: recreating footsteps, cloth and impacts in real time to picture, with props and a studio floor. It is the most physical craft in audio post.
India dubs enormously across languages, and this is high-volume technical work to a schedule rather than creative sound design.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream. Physics helps with acoustics and is not required.
A sound engineering diploma, a film school sound specialisation, or an apprenticeship in a studio.
Assistant at a recording or post studio, or boom operator on set.
Sound design, mixing, or live and broadcast audio - the three diverge quickly and pay differently.

entrance_exams.note: Not required. Private sound engineering institutes and studio apprenticeships are the normal routes, and this is one of the fields where a private course IS the entry.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance sound design and mixing, or a small home studio serving podcasts, ads and independent films. Audio post is one of the easiest crafts to run from a spare room.

ai_exposure.reason: Dubbing Engineer and Podcast Audio Editor are the exposed roles - automated dialogue cleanup, levelling and even synthetic dubbing across languages are already commercial products, and India's dubbing volume makes that a large exposure. Production Sound Mixer, Boom Operator and Foley Artist are protected by having to be in a physical space with a microphone, and Re-recording Mixer by the judgment of what a scene should sound like.

nuances.statement: This is one of the fields the entrance-gate rules were relaxed for. There is no public entrance into sound engineering worth naming - private institutes are the route, and their fees are the real barrier. FTII's sound specialisation is the exception and takes a handful of students a year.

professions.one_liner: Records what is in front of the lens - weddings, products, wildlife, news, people.

deviating_roles.why: Wedding work is people management as much as photography - reading a family, working fourteen-hour days and never getting a second chance at a moment. It is also where most of the money in Indian photography actually is.
Wildlife work is fieldcraft and patience - days of waiting, alone, in conditions nobody else would choose. The subject cannot be directed.
Retouching is desk work in software, and it is the part of the profession most directly exposed to generative tools.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
A photography diploma or apprenticeship with a working photographer. Neither is required.
A camera and lenses - the real capital cost of this profession, and the reason cost_of_entry is not near zero.
Second shooter at a wedding studio, assistant at a commercial studio, or direct client work.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Own studio or freelance practice, which is what almost all Indian photography is. Wedding work is the volume market and a photographer running a small team through a season earns well above the employed figure.

ai_exposure.reason: Split sharply. Product & Advertising Photographer and Photo Editor & Retoucher are directly exposed - synthetic product imagery is already replacing catalogue shoots, and retouching is largely automated. Wedding Photographer, Event Videographer and Wildlife Photographer are nearly untouched, because the job is to be physically present while something real and unrepeatable happens.

nuances.statement: The employed range badly understates this profession, because there is barely an employed version of it. Almost all Indian photographers are self-employed and wedding season income is concentrated into a few months. The number to look at is self_employment.route, not mid_career_lpa.

Photojournalist is deliberately NOT listed here - it sits under Journalist & Reporter, because the object of concern there is the news, and a photojournalist answers to an editor and a standard of evidence rather than to a client.

professions.one_liner: Builds the world a story is filmed in - sets, locations, props, the look of the place.

deviating_roles.why: Finding and securing locations is negotiation, permissions and logistics with landowners, police and municipalities. It is the least visual job in a visual department.
These are workshop and site trades - carpentry, scenic painting, sourcing and maintaining hundreds of physical objects to a shooting schedule.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Architecture, interior design, fine art or film school - all four are common routes. None is required.
Art department assistant, then set decorator or art director. Entry is through the department, not through a qualification.
Production designer on ads, series and films.

entrance_exams.note: Not required.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance per project, like the rest of a film crew. Many art directors also take event, exhibition and retail-display work between films, which smooths the income.

ai_exposure.reason: Concept Artist (Film) is the exposed role, for the same reason illustration is - visual development boards are exactly what image models produce. Everything downstream is protected by physical construction: a set has to be built, dressed, lit and walked through by actors, and Set Construction Supervisor, Prop Master and Location Manager are craft and negotiation jobs in the real world.

nuances.statement: Promised to this sector from Sector 8 rather than kept with Interior Designer, and the substitution test is why: remove the film and nothing survives. A set exists to be photographed from specific angles for a story - it does not have to be lived in, does not have to last, and often has no fourth wall.

professions.one_liner: Makes and publishes their own video, audio or writing to an audience they built themselves.

deviating_roles.why: These are the paid JOBS inside the creator economy rather than creator careers - running comments, sponsorships, scheduling and edits for someone else's channel. They are salaried, unlike the rest of the profession.
Audio and text formats reward depth and consistency over performance, and build smaller, more durable audiences than short-form video does.
Live and short-form work is continuous public performance with immediate feedback. It is the highest-visibility and least stable end of the profession.

path_to_entry.requirement: None.
Publish consistently for one to two years before any income appears. This unpaid period is the real cost of entry.
Reach the platform thresholds for monetisation, and more importantly an audience a sponsor will pay to reach.
Brand deals, platform revenue, affiliate income and own products. Salaried roles exist on the operations side.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: This profession IS self-employment for almost everyone in it - brand sponsorships, platform revenue share, affiliate sales and own products. The salaried version is working on someone else's channel.

ai_exposure.reason: Both attacked and enabled by the same tools. Short-Form Video Creator faces the sharpest exposure: synthetic video and voice make the format cheap to flood, which devalues volume while raising the value of a recognisable person. Video Essayist, Podcaster and Newsletter Writer are protected by parasocial trust - the audience is there for a specific human, which is the one thing a model cannot supply. Creator Operations Assistant is exposed on the editing and scheduling side.

nuances.statement: The most dispersed income distribution in the dataset, worse even than Entrepreneur in Sector 5. A tiny number earn very large sums, a thin middle earns a living, and the overwhelming majority earn nothing at all. A range is close to meaningless here and should be read as such.

High demand for CREATORS is not the same as high probability of succeeding as one. Brand spending on creators is genuinely growing fast; the number of people competing for it is growing faster. This is the DECISIONS.md 8.45 error in its most seductive form.

None, and it is the only profession in this sector with no gatekeeper of any kind - no employer, no editor, no client. That is precisely why the failure rate is what it is: nothing filters entry, so everything filters outcome.

economics.distribution is 'power_law', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. A tiny number earn very large sums, a thin middle earns a living, and the overwhelming majority earn nothing. There is no middle to average. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it.

admin_review.reason: The economics are not describable by a range and should probably not be shown as one. Outcomes follow a power law, survivorship bias in every available source is extreme, and no Indian survey of creator earnings was found. Decide whether to suppress the numbers and state the risk instead, as was proposed for Entrepreneur in Sector 5, and whether this record should surface for school-age users at all.

professions.one_liner: Works with the voice - dubbing, narration, radio, hosting, commentary and announcements.

deviating_roles.why: Commentary is live, continuous, unscripted speech over an event you cannot control, carrying statistics and history in your head. It is the hardest live-voice job there is.
Dubbing is matching an existing performance in another language to exact lip timing. It is technical mimicry under a stopwatch, and India does it at enormous volume.
Presenting is personality on demand for hours, with an audience that is not in the room. It is performance rather than craft.

path_to_entry.requirement: None.
Voice and diction training, a radio jockeying course, or theatre. None is required; casting is on the voice.
A demo reel of two or three minutes across styles. This is the whole audition in voice work.
Dubbing studios, radio stations, e-learning and advertising voiceover, or live presenting.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance voice work booked per session or per hour, usually through studios and casting agents. A treated home booth is now enough to compete for remote sessions.

ai_exposure.reason: The most directly threatened profession in this sector, and the reason is specific: synthetic voice is commercially deployed and improving fast. E-learning Voiceover Artist, Announcer and Narrator & Audiobook Reader are the exposed roles - all three produce clean read-aloud text, which is exactly what voice models do. Dubbing Artist sits in the middle: automated cross-language dubbing exists but lip-sync performance in Indian languages is still hard. Sports Commentator, Radio Jockey and Television Presenter are protected because the audience is there for a live person reacting in real time.

nuances.statement: Rated medium rather than high on the composition, but a student should read the reason before taking comfort from the band. This is the one profession in the sector where a named commercial technology substitutes for the core output rather than for the surrounding work.

professions.one_liner: Decides what an organisation says in public, and gets it said - press, crisis, reputation.

deviating_roles.why: Speechwriting is solitary craft in someone else's voice - the opposite of the relationship-driven rest of the profession.
Crisis work is judgment under legal and reputational risk, usually at speed and out of hours. It is the highest-consequence version of this job and pays accordingly.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree; mass communication, English, political science and management are all common.
PR agency account executive, or in-house corporate communications. Agency-side is the usual training ground.
Media relations, internal communications, public affairs or crisis - they pay very differently.

entrance_exams.note: None is required. This profession hires on writing ability and relationships, not on an exam.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Independent communications consultancy, typically after 8-10 years, when the value is a personal network of editors and a track record in crises.

ai_exposure.reason: Press releases, media lists and boilerplate statements are already generated, and Public Relations Executive at the junior end is where that lands. What does not automate is the relationship and the judgment: Crisis Communications Specialist and Media Relations Officer depend on knowing which editor will take a call, what a regulator will accept, and what must not be said - clarity work with legal consequences attached.

nuances.statement: A genuinely arguable placement, flagged for sign-off. Under DECISIONS.md 2.05 the object of concern for Sector 5 is 'the organisation and its customers', which would put PR there. It sits in Sector 9 because the craft is media - shaping a story and placing it with people who publish - and because a student choosing between journalism and PR is choosing between two sides of the same trade.

High and structurally growing, for an unattractive reason: the more public scrutiny an organisation faces, the more it spends on managing what is said about it. This profession grows when trust falls.

professions.one_liner: The crew that makes a shoot physically happen - rigging, grip, power, sets, studio floor.

deviating_roles.why: Broadcast operations is technical shift work in a control room or a van - signal chains, playout and live transmission. It is salaried and rostered, unlike the day-rate crew roles, and it is the one part of this profession with a career ladder that does not require moving into another job entirely.

path_to_entry.requirement: None for crew roles. Broadcast operations usually wants a diploma in electronics or media technology.
On-the-job. Most crew enter through someone they know on a unit; broadcast operations enters through an ITI or polytechnic diploma.
Day-rate crew on shoots and events, or a rostered post at a broadcaster or studio.
Move into a department - camera, lighting, grip or broadcast engineering - which is where pay starts to separate.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Owning equipment and hiring it out with yourself attached - lights, grip gear or a camera package. This is the standard way crew income rises in Indian film and events, and it is capital, not promotion.

ai_exposure.reason: Almost unexposed, and for the plainest reason in the model: this is physical work in an unstructured space. Nothing generative rigs a light, lays a dolly track or loads a van. Broadcast Master Control Operator is the one role with real exposure, because automated playout has already reduced how many people a transmission needs.

nuances.statement: The base layer of the film and television industry, and the pay reflects that: it fails the compensation filter. Work is per-day, seasonal and almost entirely informal, with no contract and no notice. The record shows this honestly rather than dressing up glamour-adjacent work as a career.

Moderate and concentrated geographically. Essentially all of this employment is in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kochi and increasingly Noida - a student outside those cities cannot enter this profession without moving.

admin_review.reason: No sourced figure exists for Indian film crew day rates, which are the only number that matters in this profession, and none for what equipment ownership earns - the route by which crew income actually rises. Both are needed before this record can be trusted, and at 4.2 LPA employed it currently reads as a dead end.

professions.one_liner: Performs music for a living - on stage, in a studio, at a temple, or at a wedding.

deviating_roles.why: Session and accompaniment work is serving someone else's performance, note-perfect, first take, without being noticed. It is the steadiest paid work in music and the least visible.
These are public-facing careers built on a recognisable voice and a personal audience. The skill is the same; the career is a completely different gamble.
Indian classical training is a decade or more of guru-shishya study before public performance. It is the longest apprenticeship in this dataset and it is unpaid.

path_to_entry.requirement: None. Serious training almost always starts in childhood, well before class 11.
Guru-shishya study, a music school, or a BA/MA in music at a university. Years, not months - classical training runs a decade.
Optional but useful: an Akashvani audition grade, which opens broadcast bookings. It licenses nothing.
Performance, session work, accompaniment, recording and teaching - almost every working musician does several of these.

entrance_exams.note: Neither is required to work. The Akashvani audition awards a broadcast grade rather than permission to perform.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Performance fees, session work, private teaching and recording, usually all at once. Practically every Indian musician is self-employed and assembles an income from three or four sources rather than one.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure and the reason is specific: what is bought here is a live human performing in a room, and generated audio does not substitute for that. Where exposure does bite is recorded and functional music - Session Musician work on advertising beds and library music is the role most at risk, because that market buys a sound rather than a performer. Classical Vocalist, Accompanist and Devotional & Temple Musician are essentially untouched.

nuances.statement: Null, and the Sangeet Natak Akademi is not one despite being the apex body. It funds, documents and honours; it does not examine or register. The Akashvani grading system is the closest thing to a professional standard and it is voluntary - it opens broadcast bookings and bars nothing.

Six is a conservative reading and applies to the point of earning, not competence. Indian classical training routinely runs ten to fifteen years from a start in childhood, unpaid throughout, which makes it the longest and least-visible runway in this dataset.

The employed range describes salaried orchestra, ensemble and institutional posts, of which India has very few. It is close to fiction for most of this profession, where income is per performance, per session and per student. That is why the admin_review is required rather than optional.

admin_review.reason: There is no employed version of this profession at any scale in India, so mid_career_lpa - which is EMPLOYED-ONLY by design - describes almost nobody. No sourced figure exists for performance fees, session rates or private tuition income, which is where the entire livelihood sits. This is the sharpest case in the dataset of the schema's salary format failing a profession, and it recurs across most of Sector 10.

professions.one_liner: Writes and builds the music itself - for film, advertising, artists and their own releases.

deviating_roles.why: Writing words for music is a literary craft, and in India often in a language the composer does not write in. Many lyricists play no instrument at all.
Mixing is technical judgment about frequency, dynamics and space, done to serve someone else's record. It is engineering that requires musical ears.
Scoring is writing to picture on someone else's deadline and to a director's brief. The music is a service to a scene, which is a different job from writing a song.

path_to_entry.requirement: None.
Musical training plus production software. Formal music-production courses exist; most producers are self-taught on the tools.
Released or placed work. In music production credits are the only currency.
Assisting an established composer, advertising and jingle work, or independent releases and artist production.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Per-project fees, royalties and a home studio. Advertising and corporate work is what pays the bills between the projects people enter this profession for.

ai_exposure.reason: The most exposed profession in this sector by a wide margin, and unusually the threat is to the paying middle rather than the entry rung. Generative audio already produces usable library music, advertising beds and background loops, which is exactly what Jingle Composer, Music Programmer and much Arranger work is. Film Music Composer and Background Score Composer are protected by having to serve a director, a scene and a deadline through revisions - and Lyricist by writing in a specific Indian language for a specific voice.

nuances.statement: Royalty income is invisible in these figures and can be the larger half of a successful composer's earnings over time. It is also extremely uneven and arrives years late, so it cannot be represented as an annual salary.

The band is medium, but the exposure is unusually shaped: it hits FUNCTIONAL music - the anonymous score behind an advertisement or a corporate video - which is precisely the reliable commercial work that funds an Indian composer's career while they build toward film and artist projects.

professions.one_liner: Performs and creates dance - classical, film, contemporary, folk and commercial.

deviating_roles.why: Choreography for screen is directing bodies to camera on a schedule, with dozens of dancers and a producer's budget. It is leadership and logistics as much as movement.
Classical forms carry repertoire, mythology and abhinaya learned over a decade or more. The performance is interpretive rather than physical display.
Movement direction shapes how actors inhabit their bodies in a play or film. It is coaching and analysis, and the movement director rarely performs.

path_to_entry.requirement: None. Classical training generally starts in childhood.
Years under a guru, a dance school, or a BA/MA in dance at an institution such as Kalakshetra or Rabindra Bharati.
Arangetram or equivalent debut for classical forms; auditions and troupe work for commercial dance.
Performance, troupe membership, film and event work, choreography and teaching - nearly always several at once.

entrance_exams.note: Not required to perform. Degrees in dance exist and matter mainly for teaching posts, which belong to Sector 12.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Performance fees, film and event bookings, and running a dance school - which in practice is what most classical dancers do, and it is the part that pays reliably.

ai_exposure.reason: Among the least exposed professions in the dataset. Dance is a trained body in a physical space, and no part of that is a text or image problem. Synthetic video can depict dancing; it cannot be the dancer a company hires or the choreographer who rehearses forty people. Assistant Choreographer is the only role with any exposure, through pre-visualisation tools.

nuances.statement: The employed range describes company and institutional posts, which India has very few of. It also hides a hard fact of this profession: performing income falls with age in a way most careers' do not, and teaching is not a fallback but the intended second half.

Moderate rather than low because of the volume of commercial work - film, television, weddings and events employ far more dancers than the classical concert circuit does. A student attracted by the classical form should know the paying market is mostly elsewhere.

admin_review.reason: Performance fees, event rates and dance-school income are the whole livelihood and none is sourced. The record also has nothing on the age profile of performing income, which is the single most important economic fact in a physical performance career and is currently invisible.

professions.one_liner: Plays a part in front of an audience or a camera - stage, screen, television or ad film.

deviating_roles.why: Theatre is ensemble work with months of rehearsal, a whole play held in memory and a live audience with no second take. Repertory is also the only salaried acting work in India, and it pays modestly.
Background and crowd work is long, unglamorous, poorly paid day work with no lines. It is how a large number of people in Mumbai and Hyderabad actually earn from film, and it leads nowhere by itself.
Street theatre is performance without a stage, a ticket or a captive audience, usually carrying a social message. Holding a crowd that did not choose to watch is a distinct skill.

path_to_entry.requirement: None.
Theatre groups and college drama, then optionally NSD, FTII, or a private acting school. NSD requires six prior productions just to apply.
A showreel and a photo portfolio, and registration with casting directors.
Auditions - advertising, television, web series and film. Advertising and television are where steady early income is.

entrance_exams.note: Neither is required and most working Indian actors attended neither. NSD takes 26 students a year for the whole country.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Almost universal - actors are hired per project with no employment relationship. The exceptions are repertory companies and long-running television serials, both of which offer something closer to a salary.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure on the composition, and the honest caveat is that synthetic performers are the one place this could change faster than the model suggests. Background Artist and Advertising Film Actor are the exposed roles - crowd replacement and synthetic presenters are already in commercial use. Stage Actor, Repertory Company Actor and Improv Performer are protected by the audience being in the room with a person who might fail.

nuances.statement: NSD was briefly recorded as this profession's primary_gate and has been removed on review. It takes 26 students a year nationally and almost no working Indian actor went through it, so naming it as THE gate would have told a fifteen-year-old that acting has a door 26 places wide. It does not - it has auditions, which cannot be counted. Recording a famous number because it is the only number available is the opposite of what the gate registry is for.

A power-law distribution presented as a range, which is close to misleading. A handful earn extraordinarily, a thin layer of television and advertising actors earn a living, and most people who describe themselves as actors earn very little from acting in any given year.

economics.distribution is 'power_law', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. A handful earn extraordinarily, a thin layer of television and advertising actors earn a living, and most people who describe themselves as actors earn very little from acting in any given year. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it.

admin_review.reason: Same defect as Digital Content Creator in Sector 9 and Entrepreneur in Sector 5: the income distribution is a power law and a range may be the wrong format entirely. Decide whether to suppress the numbers and state the risk. No sourced figure exists for Indian television, advertising or repertory day rates, which are the realistic income for anyone who does make a living here.

professions.one_liner: Reads a room and plays music live to it - clubs, weddings, festivals and events.

deviating_roles.why: Wedding work is equipment logistics, client management and playing what the family wants rather than what you would choose. It is also where nearly all the money in Indian DJing is.
Production is studio work made alone on a screen. Many producers never perform and many performers never produce, though the industry treats them as one career.

path_to_entry.requirement: None.
Controller, speakers and a laptop. This is the real cost of entry and it is why the figure is not near zero.
Build sets and a following - mixes online, small venues, and word of mouth in a city.
Residencies, wedding and event bookings, corporate parties and festivals. Wedding season is the income.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: This profession is self-employment. Bookings are taken directly or through event agencies, and owning a full sound and lighting rig roughly doubles what a wedding booking pays.

ai_exposure.reason: Genuinely two-sided. Electronic Music Producer faces the same generative-audio pressure as the rest of music production, and automated mixing and recommendation already do a creditable job of sequencing tracks. But the paying job is not track selection - it is reading a specific room of drunk, tired or delighted people and changing course, which is why Club DJ, Wedding & Event DJ and Festival Performer are protected. A playlist has never been the competition; a playlist has always existed.

nuances.statement: High, and it rests almost entirely on the Indian wedding market rather than on club culture. That makes the work seasonal and regionally spread rather than concentrated in a few metros, which is unusual for this sector.
Wedding and event income arrives in a few months of the year and is billed per booking, not per month. Annual figures flatten a shape that a student planning cashflow needs to see.

professions.one_liner: Performs an inherited regional form - wedding bands, temple music, folk theatre, processions.

deviating_roles.why: Folk theatre and puppetry carry long narrative repertoires performed over hours, often with improvised topical commentary. The performer is a storyteller first.
Band and procession work is physically hard, seasonal and standardised - marching, carrying, playing the same repertoire. It is also the largest employer in this profession by a distance.

path_to_entry.requirement: None. Almost all of these forms are learned within a family or community from childhood.
Apprenticeship within the tradition. Some forms have state academies and guru-shishya schemes funded through the Sangeet Natak Akademi and state culture departments.
Weddings, festivals, temple calendars and processions - work follows the season and the local ritual year.
State and national culture-department empanelment, festival circuits and grants, which is what lifts a folk performer above local rates.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Performing on own account or as part of a family troupe, taking bookings directly. The step that actually changes income is empanelment with a state culture department or a festival circuit, which converts local rates into touring fees.

ai_exposure.reason: The lowest exposure in this sector along with dance, and for the same reason: the work is a human body performing in a physical place, usually as part of a ritual or a celebration whose whole point is that people are present. Recorded music substitutes for a wedding band at the cheap end of the market, but that substitution happened decades ago and is not new.

nuances.statement: The base layer of Indian performing arts, and the numbers say so. Income is per booking, seasonal, cash and undocumented. This fails the compensation filter, which is correct, and it is listed anyway because it is where a very large number of performing livelihoods actually are.

Moderate and structurally uneven. Ritual and wedding demand is steady and geographically spread; the audience for long-form folk theatre is shrinking as television and phones absorb the evenings it used to fill. Those two facts point opposite ways and both are true.

Placed here rather than in Sector 17 with heritage because these are working performers being paid to perform, not custodians interpreting a tradition for study. The intervene-versus-interpret split in DECISIONS.md 2 is what decides it.

admin_review.reason: No sourced income figure exists for any Indian folk performance work - not wedding band rates, not troupe fees, not state empanelment payments. Empanelment is named as the route by which income rises and its value is unknown, which makes the most important advice on this record unquantified.

professions.one_liner: Makes a live show work - sound, lights, rigging, staging and the running of the event.

deviating_roles.why: Running a show is schedule, communication and problem-solving under a clock that cannot be stopped. It is the management job inside a technical department.
Rigging carries genuine physical risk - trusses, motors and points over people's heads. It is the one role here where a mistake injures someone.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream, or none. Physics helps with sound and electricity.
A sound or event-technology diploma, or entry as stage crew and learning on the job. Both routes are normal.
Crew for an event production or sound-hire company. Work is per show and heavily seasonal.
Front-of-house sound, monitors, lighting or rigging. Specialising is what separates day-rate crew from booked engineers.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Owning equipment - a PA system, lighting rig or backline - and hiring it out with yourself operating it. Equipment ownership, not seniority, is how income rises in live production.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure. Mixing a live band in a room with feedback, a bad PA and a singer who moves is a real-time physical problem, and automated mixing tools assume a studio. AV Technician is the most exposed role, since corporate AV is increasingly pre-programmed and automated. Stage Rigger and Backline Technician are untouched - the work is hardware in the air and on the floor.

nuances.statement: High and growing, driven by live events, weddings, corporate conferences and a genuine festival circuit that did not exist fifteen years ago. This is the most reliably employable profession in Sector 10 and the least visible.

Certificate, and the honest note is that the diploma matters less than the first crew job. Live production hires people it has seen work, which makes entry easy for anyone near a city with events and nearly impossible remotely.

professions.one_liner: Builds, tunes and repairs instruments - sitars, tablas, harmoniums, guitars, pianos.

deviating_roles.why: Piano tuning is an acoustic and mechanical discipline with an objective standard, practised on other people's instruments in their homes. It is a service call, not workshop making.
Building a stringed instrument is woodwork with an acoustic result you cannot see - choosing timber by how it rings. It is the longest-apprenticed craft in this profession.

path_to_entry.requirement: None. The trade is usually inherited or entered as a workshop apprentice.
Apprenticeship in a making workshop - Miraj, Kolkata, Delhi and Chennai are the main Indian centres.
Making or repairing for a workshop, a music shop or a distributor.
Own workshop, which is where the difference between a wage and a livelihood is in this trade.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.
