self_employment.route: Own workshop making to order and repairing, selling direct to musicians and shops. A maker with a name among performers charges several times what workshop wages pay.

ai_exposure.reason: Essentially unexposed. Instrument making is skilled handwork on natural materials judged by ear, and repair is diagnosis of a physical object in front of you. Nothing in the generative-AI wave touches any part of it. The threats to this trade are real but entirely different: cheap imported factory instruments and a shrinking number of apprentices.

nuances.statement: Low, and it is a thin but stable market rather than a collapsing one. The number of makers is falling faster than demand, which is why skilled repairers are genuinely scarce in most Indian cities - a student entering this trade competes with very few people.

Workshop wages and an independent maker's income are barely the same profession. The employed figure is the floor; the route out of it is a reputation among performers, which takes years and is not purchasable.

admin_review.reason: No sourced income figure for Indian instrument makers or repairers, employed or independent, and the gap between the two is the whole story of this trade. At 4.8 LPA employed with a named independent route and no ceiling, the record currently understates it in exactly the way self_employment.ceiling_lpa was added to prevent.

professions.one_liner: Makes theatre happen - directing, writing plays, producing and running a company.

deviating_roles.why: Writing for the stage is solitary and slow, and in India frequently involves translating or adapting across languages. The playwright is rarely in the rehearsal room.

Applied theatre uses drama in schools, prisons, hospitals and community work. The goal is the participants' change rather than a performance, and it is the most reliably funded work in this profession.
Producing is budgets, venues, grants, sponsorship and touring. Indian theatre companies survive on this work and it is nothing like directing.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree - NSD requires one in any discipline to apply, plus six prior productions.
NSD, a university drama department, or years inside a working theatre group. The group route is the commonest.
Directing for a company, applied theatre and workshop facilitation, and grant-funded productions. Very few make a living from productions alone.

entrance_exams.note: Not required. NSD takes 26 students a year nationally and most theatre practitioners in India trained inside a group instead.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Running a company or working project to project on grants, commissions, corporate workshops and applied theatre contracts. Workshop and facilitation work is what most Indian theatre-makers actually live on.

ai_exposure.reason: The lowest digital exposure in the dataset alongside the trades, and the highest clarity in this sector. The job is deciding what a play should mean now, to this audience, in this city - then getting thirty people to agree and rehearse it. Playwright is the only role with real exposure, and even there the constraint is that a play must survive being spoken aloud by actors for two hours.

nuances.statement: Low, and honestly so. India has few funded theatre companies, almost no commercial theatre outside a handful of cities, and shrinking state culture budgets. The work exists and is done; it is rarely a whole income, and applied theatre and corporate workshops are what make it viable.

Understated even by this sector's standards, because grant-funded and commission income is lumpy and most practitioners hold a second job. The figures assume a practice subsidised by facilitation and workshop work, which is the normal case.

admin_review.reason: No sourced figure for Indian theatre grant, commission or facilitation rates, which are the actual income here. The record also cannot show what proportion of practitioners hold a second job, which for this profession is the most decision-relevant fact there is.

professions.one_liner: The person in the photograph or on the ramp - the presence is the product.

deviating_roles.why: Fit modelling is technical and repetitive - standing for hours while garments are adjusted to a body that matches a size standard. It is the one role here that is steady, private and paid by the hour rather than by visibility.

path_to_entry.requirement: A portfolio, a comp card and physical criteria set by the client. There is no course and no qualification
Registration with a modelling agency, or direct casting calls
Portfolio built through test shoots, then paid catalogue and commercial work
Ramp, campaign and brand work for the small number who reach it

entrance_exams.note: No entrance examination exists and no institution certifies a model. Agencies and casting directors are the gate, and their criteria are physical and commercial.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Almost every model is independent - paid per shoot or per show, through an agency that takes a commission, with no employment relationship. There is no salaried version of this work.

ai_exposure.reason: The exposure model here measures retrievable knowledge and digital skill, and by that measure modelling scores low because the work is physical presence. That understates a real and already-arrived threat: generative image models are replacing catalogue and e-commerce modelling, where the client needs a body wearing a garment and does not need it to be a particular person. Ramp, campaign and celebrity-adjacent work is far less substitutable.

nuances.statement: Performing Arts & Music, beside Actor & Performer, because in both the person IS the instrument and the work is presence in front of an audience or a camera. Two alternatives were considered: Sector 8 beside Fashion Designer, rejected because a model designs nothing; and Sector 9 beside Voice Artist & Broadcast Presenter, which is defensible and was not chosen because ramp work is not media production.

There is no annual salary for this work and quoting one would be false. What is sourced is PER-ENGAGEMENT: roughly 2,000 to 30,000 rupees per shoot for most commercial work in India, with international brand campaigns reaching a lakh and above, from an Indian modelling platform's published rate guide. The annual bands here are that per-shoot rate multiplied by an assumed and unsourced number of bookings, which is why distribution is power_law and an admin_review is open.

The low band is correct by this repo's model and misleading on its own. Generative image tools are already substituting for catalogue and e-commerce modelling - the segment where most working models actually earn - because the client needs a garment shown on a body, not a specific person. The composition model cannot express substitution of a physical presence by a generated image, and the application should carry that warning from this nuance rather than from the band.

Booking-to-booking independent work with an agency commission is the normal arrangement, not the exception. There is no employed version of this profession to compare against, which is part of why the earnings bands describe nobody in particular.

admin_review.reason: economics.distribution is power_law and the bands are a per-shoot rate multiplied by an assumed booking frequency that is not sourced. A handful of models earn very large sums, a thin layer earn a living from catalogue and commercial work, and most people who describe themselves as models earn very little from modelling in any given year. Decide how the application presents this - and note the second risk on the record: generative image models are already displacing the catalogue segment that most working models depend on.

professions.one_liner: Competes in a sport for a living - through a league, a federation, or a sports quota job.

deviating_roles.why: Both are competitive sports in which physical output is nearly irrelevant and concentration under long pressure is everything. Chess in particular has a career shape unlike any other sport here - it starts earlier and lasts far longer.
The league sports. These are the only three in India with genuine professional contracts and public visibility, which changes both the money and the pressure.

Para sport carries the same training demands with a fraction of the funding, the coaching infrastructure and the commercial attention - and a classification system that can reclassify an athlete out of their event.

Motorsport is spatial judgment and reaction at speed with a real and continuous risk of injury, sustained for hours. A rally co-driver does not drive at all - they read pace notes aloud at the exact moment the driver needs them, which is a navigation and nerve discipline of its own.

path_to_entry.requirement: None. Serious training starts in childhood; by class 11 an athlete is usually already competing at state level.
Academy, SAI centre, Khelo India centre or a private club. Selection is by performance at district and state meets.
Place in National Championships, National Games or Category A/B/C championships - this is what unlocks both selection and the sports quota.
A league contract in cricket, football or kabaddi; or - far more commonly - a sports quota post in the railways, police, a bank or the armed forces.

public_routes: Sports quota recruitment (Railways, police, banks, PSUs)
entrance_exams.note: There is no entrance examination. The qualifying currency is a sporting placing, and the sports quota converts it into a permanent government job.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Prize money, appearance fees, coaching and endorsements - and for most athletes outside the three league sports, none of these is the main income. The sports quota government post is.

ai_exposure.reason: Among the least exposed professions in the dataset. Sport is a human body competing against another human body and an audience that wants to watch people do it. Nothing generative touches the work. Chess Player is the one genuine exception in a sense no other profession faces: engines have been superhuman for decades, and the game survived because the market was never for the best moves but for people playing.

nuances.statement: The single most misunderstood record in this sector. Outside cricket, football and kabaddi, an Indian athlete's income is usually not from sport at all - it is a 7th CPC government salary obtained THROUGH sport via the sports quota, at Level 1 to Level 5. That is a modest but permanent, pensionable job, and it is a far better outcome than the word 'athlete' suggests to most families.

There is a real and brutal window that this schema field cannot hold, because it is not about age. Sports quota eligibility counts achievements from the current and previous two financial years only. An athlete who peaks at 19 and declines by 23 can be shut out of the route entirely, having given the years.

Low, and it should be read as 'very few paid places' rather than 'do not do this'. Sport at school and state level is participation; the number of people paid to compete in India is small in every discipline except cricket.

economics.distribution is 'power_law', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. Outside cricket, football and kabaddi almost nobody earns from competing. The realistic outcome is a sports quota government salary, which is a different distribution entirely. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it.

MOTORSPORT IS PAY-TO-RACE AND THE COST FIGURE ON THIS RECORD DOES NOT COVER IT. Every other athlete here has a cost of entry near 3 lakh and earns from competing. A motorsport racer BUYS THE SEAT - karting through to formula and touring car seasons are funded by the driver or by sponsorship the driver must raise themselves, and a season runs to many lakh. The income structure is inverted relative to the rest of the profession, and a family should understand that before a teenager asks for the first karting season. No sourced Indian figure for a season's cost was found, which is why it is stated as a shape rather than a number.

admin_review.reason: Two gaps. First, this is a power-law income like Actor and Digital Content Creator, and a range misrepresents it. Second and more fixable: the sports quota route is the realistic outcome for most athletes and the record has no sourced figure for what a Level 1 to Level 5 railway post actually pays in hand. That number exists - it is on the 7th CPC matrix - and until it is fetched the most likely outcome of this career is unquantified. A third gap has been added: motorsport is PAY-TO-RACE and this record's cost_of_entry_lakh of 3.0 does not describe it at all. A sourced figure for an Indian karting or formula season is needed, and if it is as far outside the range as expected, Motorsport Racer may need to leave this record for one of its own.

professions.one_liner: Trains athletes and teams to perform - technique, tactics, conditioning and selection.

deviating_roles.why: These are applied physiology roles - load management, testing and injury return protocols. The work is programme design and measurement rather than technique on the field, and it sits closest to sports science.
Scouting is judgment about who a fourteen-year-old will become, made from watching hundreds of them. It is prediction, and the coach never trains most of the people they assess.
Coaching children is about keeping them in the sport, managing parents and building confidence. Winning is not the objective, which inverts the rest of the profession.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream. Most coaches come from having played the sport.
NSNIS Patiala diploma or certificate in sports coaching, a federation coaching licence, or a BPEd/MPEd. None is legally required.
Sport-specific federation licences - AIFF and BCCI run graded levels. These are what clubs and academies actually ask for.
Academy, school, club, state association or SAI centre; or private coaching on your own account.

public_routes: Sports quota recruitment (Railways, police, banks, PSUs)
private_entrances: Federation coaching licences (AIFF, BCCI and others)
entrance_exams.note: None is legally required to coach. Federation licences are contractual requirements set by employers and competitions, not statutory ones.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Private coaching, running an academy, or personal coaching of individual athletes. An academy with fifty paying children earns more reliably than most salaried coaching posts.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure. Coaching is watching a specific body move, knowing what is wrong, and getting a person to change a habit under pressure - none of which is a text problem. Team Analyst is the exposed role: video tagging and statistical breakdown is already largely automated, and what survives is the interpretation. Grassroots & Youth Coach is the safest work here and also the largest employer.

nuances.statement: A genuinely arguable placement. DECISIONS.md 2 sends teaching-anything to Sector 12, and a coach clearly teaches. It sits here because the object of concern is COMPETITIVE PERFORMANCE rather than learning: a coach is accountable for whether the athlete wins, selects the squad, and manages injury and load. A Physical Education Teacher, who is accountable for a curriculum and a class, is routed to Sector 12 instead.

Null, and worth stating plainly because the National Sports Governance Act 2025 has just created new statutory machinery. That Act regulates federations, tribunals and elections - it licenses no coach. Federation coaching licences are real gates but they are contractual, set by employers and competitions.

professions.one_liner: Gets ordinary people fitter and keeps them safe doing it - gyms, studios, homes, online.

deviating_roles.why: Online coaching is programme writing, check-ins and accountability by message. The trainer never touches the client, which removes the safety role that defines the rest of the profession.
Training older adults and people with medical conditions is caution-led work with real clinical risk, done in close coordination with physiotherapists and doctors.
Leading a room of thirty people to music is performance. The instructor motivates a crowd rather than correcting an individual.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream, or none. Most certifying bodies require class 12 or equivalent.
A personal training certification - SPEFL-SC / NSQF aligned, or an international body. Gyms ask for one; no law does.
Gym floor instructor, then personal training clients. Almost all Indian gym trainers start salaried and move to commission.
Own client roster, a studio, or online coaching - where the income actually changes.

private_entrances: Personal training certifications (SPEFL-SC, ACE, ACSM and others)
entrance_exams.note: No public entrance exists. Certification is a private market and the qualification employers ask for is set by the gym, not by statute.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Personal training clients taken directly, a small studio, or online coaching. Trainers with a full private roster earn multiples of the gym floor salary, which is why almost everyone in this profession is trying to get there.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure with one clear crack. Online Fitness Coach is directly exposed - generating a training programme from goals, height and weight is exactly what a model does well, and app based coaching already competes on price. What survives is presence: spotting a failing squat, adjusting a grip, and being the reason someone turned up at six in the morning. Personal Trainer and Senior & Special Population Trainer are protected by touch and liability.

nuances.statement: High and genuinely growing - urban gym membership, corporate wellness and post-pandemic health awareness have all expanded the market. This is the most reliably employable profession in Sector 11 and the one with the lowest barrier to entry, which also means the most competition.

Null, and this is a real consumer-safety gap rather than a neutral fact. Anyone in India may call themselves a personal trainer and take money to load a stranger's spine. Certification is entirely a private market with no floor.

professions.one_liner: Runs the competition itself - refereeing, umpiring, judging, timing and scoring.

deviating_roles.why: Judging gymnastics, diving or boxing is applying a written code to a movement seen once, in seconds, with no replay in most Indian competition. It is assessment rather than enforcement.
On-field officiating is authority under open hostility from players, coaches and a crowd, while physically keeping up with the game. Being liked is not part of it.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
State or national federation officiating examination for the sport - BCCI's umpiring levels, AIFF referee courses and their equivalents.
Get onto a district, then state, then national panel. Progression is by assessment on matches actually officiated.
Match fees per fixture. Only the top national panels in cricket offer anything resembling a full income.

public_routes: Federation officiating examinations (BCCI, AIFF and others)
entrance_exams.note: These are federation examinations, not statutory ones - they control who may officiate that federation's competitions and nothing beyond it.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Match fees, which is how essentially all officiating is paid. Officials at the top of a national panel in cricket earn a real income; everyone below that is doing it alongside another job.

ai_exposure.reason: Genuinely contested, and this is the one profession in Sector 11 where technology has already taken work. Timekeeper & Scorer is substantially automated, and ball tracking, goal-line technology and video review have moved decisions away from the on-field official in every sport that can afford them. What remains is the part machines cannot do: managing twenty-two angry people, applying judgment where the code is silent, and being the person accountable for the call.

nuances.statement: Match-fee income, and for almost everyone in this profession it is a second income rather than a livelihood. The wide mid-career range is the gap between a district panel official officiating on weekends and a national panel cricket umpire.

Low in paid terms and steady in real terms - every competition needs officials and India is chronically short of qualified ones, particularly in women's sport and outside cricket. Scarcity here has not translated into pay.

admin_review.reason: No sourced figure for Indian match fees at any level, in any sport, and match fees are the entire income of this profession. At 4.9 LPA mid-career with a named self-employment route and no ceiling, the record cannot distinguish a weekend district official from a national panel umpire - which is the only distinction that matters here.

professions.one_liner: Takes people safely into mountains, rivers and the sea, and teaches them to move there.

deviating_roles.why: Outdoor education runs school and corporate programmes where the objective is confidence, teamwork or leadership. The activity is a vehicle; the client is usually frightened and unfit.
Both operate under international certifying bodies with strict procedural discipline and equipment checks, where a missed step is fatal rather than embarrassing.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Basic and Advanced Mountaineering courses at NIM Uttarkashi, HMI Darjeeling or another government institute; or international certification for diving and paragliding.
Logged days - summits, dives, river descents or flights. This is what actually qualifies you in the eyes of an employer.
Adventure tour operators, outdoor education companies, or your own operation. Work is seasonal and tied to a specific geography.

public_routes: Mountaineering course admission (NIM, HMI and state institutes)
private_entrances: Scuba and paragliding certifications (PADI, SSI and equivalents)
entrance_exams.note: Government mountaineering institutes run the main Indian courses and are heavily oversubscribed; diving and flying are certified by international private bodies, which are the only real route in those disciplines.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Running your own trips, or a small operation with equipment. Owning gear - boats, ropes, dive kit - is what separates a guide on a day rate from an operator taking the margin.

ai_exposure.reason: Essentially unexposed, and one of the clearest cases in the model of physical skill in an unstructured environment being a moat rather than a liability. Route-finding, reading weather, judging whether a client can continue and rescuing them when they cannot are all decisions made with a body in a place. No role here has meaningful exposure.

nuances.statement: Moderate and concentrated - this work exists in Uttarakhand, Himachal, Ladakh, the Northeast, Goa and the Andamans and almost nowhere else. It is also strongly seasonal, so a full year's income usually means following the season across two regions or holding a winter job.

Placed here rather than in Sector 16 with travel because the object of concern is physical performance and safety in a demanding environment, not hospitality. Adventure tourism is the EMPLOYER, and DECISIONS.md 2.2 says an employer is a tag.

professions.one_liner: Competes or works professionally in organised competitive video gaming.

deviating_roles.why: Broadcast roles are live commentary and vision-mixing over a match nobody controls. They are the most transferable jobs in esports and the only ones with an obvious career outside it.
Coaching and analysis in esports is drafting, strategy and reviewing recorded matches frame by frame. It is closer to a chess second than to a sports coach on a field.

path_to_entry.requirement: None.
Reach the top competitive ranks of a title with an Indian scene. This is public and verifiable, which makes entry unusually meritocratic.
Join an organised roster and compete in qualifiers and tournaments.
Team salary and prize money, streaming income, or the non-playing roles - coaching, casting, tournament operations.

entrance_exams.note: None. Ranking is the only qualification and it is public.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Streaming and content alongside competing, which is how most Indian esports players actually earn. Prize money alone supports very few.

ai_exposure.reason: The most exposed profession in Sector 11 and the reason is unusual: the competitive titles themselves are AI-adjacent, and the surrounding jobs are digital. Team Analyst (Esports) is directly exposed - match review and draft analysis is pattern recognition over recorded data. Professional Player is protected in the same way Chess Player is: the audience is watching humans compete, and superhuman bots have existed in several titles for years without affecting that at all.

nuances.statement: Low, and this needs saying bluntly because it is one of the most aspired-to careers among Indian teenagers. India has a very large gaming AUDIENCE and a very small number of paid competitive places - perhaps a few hundred salaried players nationally across all titles. Reading audience size as opportunity is the DECISIONS.md 8.45 error in its most tempting form.

A power-law distribution again, and with a shorter career than any other profession in this dataset - competitive playing careers commonly end in the mid-twenties. The non-playing roles are the realistic long-term work and they pay less than the equivalent job outside esports.

Two years is the time to reach a competitive roster, not a qualification - there is none. What the number hides is that the training is thousands of hours of play with no transferable credential at the end if it does not work out.

economics.distribution is 'power_law', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. A few hundred paid roster places nationally against a very large amateur population, and a playing career that commonly ends in the mid-twenties. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it.

admin_review.reason: Aspiration-to-reality gap is the widest in the dataset. No sourced figure exists for Indian esports salaries, prize distribution or the number of paid roster spots, and every one of those is needed before this record can be shown to a fifteen-year-old. Decide also whether the very short playing career should be surfaced as a structural warning rather than left in a nuance.

professions.one_liner: Measures what athletes do and turns it into training decisions - physiology, biomechanics, data.

deviating_roles.why: Performance psychology is conversation and behavioural work with an athlete under pressure. It shares an employer with the rest of this profession and almost no method.
Analysis is video, tracking data and statistics rather than laboratory physiology. It is the fastest-growing part of the profession and the most portable outside sport.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream; Biology and Physical Education help for the physiology route.
BSc/MSc in Sports Science, Exercise Physiology, or a BPEd/MPEd. Data-side entrants often come from statistics or computing.
SAI centre, national federation, a professional club, or a private high-performance facility.
Physiology, biomechanics, analysis or psychology - they diverge quickly and only analysis transfers easily outside sport.

entrance_exams.note: Neither is required. Sports science degrees are a normal university admission rather than a specialist gate.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Consultancy to clubs, academies and individual athletes, usually after building a reputation inside an institution. A small private testing or analysis practice is the common form.

ai_exposure.reason: The most exposed non-esports role here. Performance Analyst and Sports Data Analyst work is video tagging, event coding and statistical modelling, and automated tracking already does most of the collection - what survives is deciding what the numbers mean for one athlete's next eight weeks. Exercise Physiologist and Biomechanist are protected by having to put sensors on a real body and interpret an individual's response.

nuances.statement: Low in India specifically, and the reason is structural: high performance support staff exist where there is money in the sport, which in India means cricket, a handful of federations and the SAI system. The skills transfer well abroad and to general healthcare, which is why pathway is 'any'.

Tagged to EXT-RND as well as SPEFL because a good deal of this work is genuine applied research. The boundary with Sector 3 is method: a sports scientist measuring an athlete to change their training is intervening, not investigating.

professions.one_liner: Prepares and maintains where sport is played - pitches, courts, pools, tracks and gyms.

deviating_roles.why: Preparing a cricket pitch is agronomy with a competitive outcome attached - soil, moisture, rolling and grass judged against how the match should play. A senior curator is consulted by captains and is one of the few people in this profession with real standing.
Kit management is inventory, logistics and preparation rather than groundwork, and it travels with the team.

path_to_entry.requirement: None.
On the job under a working groundsman. Turf management courses exist and are rare; almost nobody enters through one.
Ground staff at a club, stadium, school, university or municipal facility.
Curation, turf science or facility management - the routes by which this becomes a skilled trade rather than manual work.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Contract maintenance of grounds and facilities for schools, clubs and housing societies - a small crew and equipment is the whole business, and it is how experienced ground staff raise their income.

ai_exposure.reason: Almost unexposed. Preparing a surface is outdoor physical work responding to weather, soil and use, and there is no digital output to substitute for. The one role with any exposure is Equipment & Kit Manager, through inventory software rather than through anything interesting.

nuances.statement: The base layer of the sports sector, and it fails the compensation filter. Ground staff at most Indian clubs and municipal facilities are on casual or contract terms. The exception worth knowing is that a recognised cricket pitch curator at a first class venue is a genuinely skilled and respected position.

Moderate and quietly stable - every school, club, stadium, university and gated community with a sports facility needs this work done, and the number of such facilities is growing. It is one of the few sports livelihoods available in a small town.

admin_review.reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian ground staff or curators, and no figure for what a contract maintenance operation earns - the route named as the way out of a 4.2 LPA employed ceiling. Also unresolved: whether the senior cricket curator role is sufficiently different in pay and standing to need its own treatment.

professions.one_liner: Teaches a class of children a subject, and is answerable for whether they learn it.

deviating_roles.why: Teaching four-year-olds is care, routine and play rather than subject instruction. The qualification route is different too - a nursery teacher training diploma rather than a B.Ed.
Senior secondary teaching is subject expertise under board-examination pressure, with students who are nearly adults. It is closest of all school roles to lecturing.
Accountable for a curriculum and a class rather than for competitive results, which is what separates this role from Sports Coach in Sector 11.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream. The stream decides which subject you can eventually teach, not whether you can teach.
A bachelor's degree in the subject, or D.El.Ed for primary teaching.
B.Ed (2 years) from an NCTE-recognised institution, or the integrated 4-year B.A./B.Sc B.Ed.
CTET or the state TET - a statutory minimum qualification for appointment to teach classes I to VIII.
KVS, NVS, state public service commission or state education department recruitment for government posts; direct interview for private schools.

entrance_exams.note: TET is a statutory eligibility condition rather than a competitive entrance - passing it does not get you a post, it only makes you eligible to be considered for one.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Private tuition alongside a teaching post, which is near-universal in India, or running a coaching centre. Tuition income frequently exceeds the school salary in the private-school half of this profession.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure and it is worth being precise about why, because content generation looks threatening. Lesson plans, worksheets and question banks do generate easily, and Computer Teacher and Language Teacher will feel that in preparation time. But the job is not producing material - it is holding the attention of forty children, noticing which one has stopped following, and being the adult in the room. Pre-Primary Teacher and Physical Education Teacher are the least exposed work in the sector.

nuances.statement: BIMODAL, and the single figure cannot say so. A Kendriya Vidyalaya PRT starts at roughly 8.3 lakh a year gross on the 7th CPC matrix - more than a fresh software developer - while a private school in a small town may pay 1.5 to 3 lakh for the same work. State government pay sits between the two. Which side of that gap you land on is decided by a recruitment examination, not by ability to teach.

Null, and the distinction matters. TET is a statutory ELIGIBILITY CONDITION under Section 23 of the RTE Act, not a licence: there is no register of teachers, no professional conduct jurisdiction and nobody is struck off. That is why this profession is Tier B rather than Tier A, despite the gate being real and hard.

High, and structurally so - India has a standing shortfall of qualified teachers, particularly in government schools and in science and mathematics. The shortage and the low private-sector pay coexist because they are different markets.

economics.distribution is 'bimodal', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. Two populations, not a spread. A Kendriya Vidyalaya primary teacher starts near 8.3 lakh on the 7th CPC matrix; a private school teacher in a small town may earn a fifth of that. Which one you are is decided by a recruitment examination, not by ability. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it.

admin_review.reason: economics.distribution is 'bimodal'. Two populations, not a spread. A Kendriya Vidyalaya primary teacher starts near 8.3 lakh on the 7th CPC matrix; a private school teacher in a small town may earn a fifth of that. Which one you are is decided by a recruitment examination, not by ability. Decide how the application should present this record - suppress the range and state the risk, or show both halves separately.

professions.one_liner: Teaches children with disabilities and learning differences, and adapts how they are taught.

deviating_roles.why: Early intervention works with children under six and with their parents, often delivering a diagnosis families have not accepted. The clinical and counselling content is far higher than in classroom special education.
Assistive technology is a technical specialism - devices, screen readers, Braille systems and adaptations. It is closer to rehabilitation engineering than to teaching.

Shadow support is one-to-one accompaniment of a single child inside a mainstream class. It is the commonest entry route, is usually paid by the family rather than the school, and carries no job security.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
A bachelor's degree, then B.Ed Special Education in a disability specialisation, from an RCI-recognised institution.
Enrolment on the Central Rehabilitation Register maintained by the Rehabilitation Council of India. MANDATORY - practising without it is an offence under Section 13 of the RCI Act.
Keep the CRR registration current. It is renewable, and lapsing it means you may not lawfully hold the post.
Special school, inclusive mainstream school, early intervention centre, NGO, or private practice.

entrance_exams.note: The binding requirement is not an entrance exam but RCI registration, which follows from the recognised qualification rather than from a test.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Private practice - one-to-one remediation, assessment and shadow support paid for directly by families. Extremely common, and it is where the income in this profession actually is.

ai_exposure.reason: Among the least exposed professions in the dataset once legal accountability is applied. The work is reading one specific child's response minute by minute and changing approach, with a statutory register behind the judgment. Braille & Assistive Technology Instructor is the most exposed role, since some assistive functions are increasingly built into consumer devices - but that expands what the child can do rather than replacing the person teaching them to use it.

nuances.statement: One of the very few genuinely Tier A professions outside healthcare and law. Section 13(2) of the RCI Act 1992 bars an unregistered person from holding office as, or practising as, a rehabilitation professional anywhere in India, and Section 13(3) makes contravention punishable with up to a year's imprisonment. Two limits are worth knowing: the maximum fine is Rs 1,000 and has not been revised since 1992, and Section 25 allows prosecution only on a written complaint by the Council.

High and rising, driven by the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016 and by schools being required to include children they previously excluded. The supply of RCI-registered special educators is far below what that implies, which is why shadow teaching is largely done by unregistered people - a gap the law does not acknowledge.

professions.one_liner: Teaches a subject at degree level and usually researches it - the academic career.

deviating_roles.why: Guest and contract faculty do the same teaching for a fraction of the pay, no security and no research time. In many Indian colleges they now carry most of the teaching load, and it is the realistic first job.
A postdoc is a research position with little or no teaching, on a fixed-term fellowship. It sits between Sector 3 and this one and is a holding pattern rather than a destination.
Technical and laboratory teaching is demonstration and supervision of practical work, with a diploma-level audience and an applied syllabus.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream - it decides the subject.
Bachelor's then master's in the subject, usually with at least 55 percent.
UGC NET, or CSIR-UGC NET for the sciences. Qualifying with JRF also funds a PhD.
PhD - now effectively required for a permanent university post, and 4 to 6 years long.
Assistant Professor at a college or university. Guest and contract faculty first, for most people.

entrance_exams.note: UGC NET is the eligibility gate for Assistant Professor posts nationally; states run their own SET/SLET as an alternative for state institutions.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Consultancy, textbook writing, examining and online course teaching alongside a post. Full independence is rare - the salary and the institution are the career.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure and unusually well protected, because the credential and the institution are the product. A model can explain a subject; it cannot award a degree, supervise a thesis or sit on an examination board. Academic Tutor and Guest Faculty are the exposed roles, since explanation-on-demand is exactly what students now get free. Research supervision and assessment are the durable core.

nuances.statement: Nine years from class 12 and that is the honest figure: three or four for the bachelor's, two for the master's, then a PhD of four to six. It is the longest runway in this dataset outside medicine, and unlike medicine there is no guaranteed post at the end.

CSIR-UGC NET is named as the primary gate for the same reason as in Sector 3 - the JRF stipend decides whether the PhD years are financially survivable. The humanities and social science UGC NET is a separate examination not yet in the registry, which is recorded in pending_gates.

'after_any_degree' is true but hides the real lock: the subject of your MASTER'S is the profession. Any bachelor's degree can lead here, but switching discipline after that usually means starting again from a relevant bachelor's, because most universities will not admit you to a master's in a subject you have not read.

professions.one_liner: Teaches students to pass a specific examination - JEE, NEET, UPSC, banking, boards.

deviating_roles.why: One-to-one tuition is relationship work with a single student and their parents. It is the largest and least visible part of Indian education and the easiest to enter.

Teaching two hundred students at a time to beat an examination is performance under measured results. Faculty are retained on their students' ranks, which is a harder accountability than any school teacher faces.
Content roles inside the coaching industry - writing questions and answering queries at scale. These are the entry jobs and they are the ones being automated.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream - it decides what you can teach.
A bachelor's degree in the subject. For JEE and NEET coaching an IIT or medical background is what the market actually pays for.
A demo lecture. Coaching institutes hire on classroom performance, not on qualifications.
Coaching institute faculty, an edtech company, or private tuition on your own account.

entrance_exams.note: None. This profession has no entrance of its own - it teaches other people's.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Own tuition practice or a coaching centre. This is the normal end state, and a tutor with a reputation in one town earns multiples of an institute salary.

ai_exposure.reason: Genuinely split, and the split runs through the middle of the profession. Doubt-Solving Faculty and Test & Question Setter are directly exposed - answering a doubt and generating a practice question are exactly what a model does, and edtech has already automated much of it. Private Tutor and star coaching faculty are protected by something a model cannot supply: a specific person the student and their parents trust with an outcome that decides the family's next twenty years.

nuances.statement: The widest employed range in this sector, and it is a power law rather than a spread. Coaching faculty with a track record at the top institutes earn extraordinary sums; most faculty earn ordinary teaching salaries with worse job security. The mid-career figure describes the middle of a distribution that has very little middle.

High, and it is worth naming what drives it: the coaching industry exists because the gates in DECISIONS.md's own entrance_gates registry are as narrow as they are. This profession's demand is a direct function of NEET at 18.7 applicants per seat and JEE at 23.5.

Placed in Education rather than treated as a business, because the object of concern is a student learning something. The coaching CENTRE as an enterprise is Sector 5 entrepreneurship; the person in front of the class is here.

economics.distribution is 'power_law', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. Star faculty at the top institutes earn extraordinary sums; the median is an ordinary teaching salary with worse job security. There is very little middle. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it.

admin_review.reason: A POWER-LAW INCOME presented as a range - DECISIONS.md 10 (sixteenth correction) names six such records and this was the only one not flagged. Star coaching faculty at the top institutes earn extraordinary sums and the median is an ordinary teaching salary with worse security; there is very little middle for a midpoint to describe. Decide whether to suppress the range and state the risk instead.

professions.one_liner: Looks after and teaches children under six - anganwadis, creches and preschools.

deviating_roles.why: Supervisors oversee a cluster of anganwadi centres - records, supplies, reporting and inspection. It is a graded government post with a pay scale, unlike the honorarium roles beneath it, and it is the only promotion route out of this profession.
Private preschool teaching is curriculum-led, parent-facing and urban. It shares an age group with anganwadi work and almost nothing else - different employer, different pay, different expectations.

path_to_entry.requirement: Class 10 or 12 depending on the state. Anganwadi Worker recruitment is usually class 10 or 12 pass.
State ICDS training for anganwadi posts, or a Nursery Teacher Training / Early Childhood Care and Education diploma for private preschools.
Anganwadi posts are filled by the state Women and Child Development department, usually with a local residence requirement.
Anganwadi centre, creche, or private preschool chain.

entrance_exams.note: Anganwadi recruitment is a state government process rather than a national entrance, and it is normally restricted to women resident in the local area.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: A private creche or playgroup, which needs a room and a licence rather than capital. It is the realistic route out of honorarium work for someone with the training.

ai_exposure.reason: Almost unexposed. The work is physically caring for very small children, feeding them, weighing them and keeping them safe. Nutrition & Health Educator (ICDS) and Anganwadi Supervisor carry the only exposure, through the record-keeping and reporting that has already largely moved to a phone application.

nuances.statement: Verified and grim. Anganwadi Workers are paid an HONORARIUM, not a salary - no pay scale, no increment, no pension. In Delhi that is Rs 12,720 a month including a generous state top-up; the fixed central component is a fraction of it, so the identical job pays several times less in states that add little. 13.5 lakh Anganwadi Workers and 10.2 lakh Helpers do this work.

Fails the compensation filter, and listing it anyway is the point. This is among the largest single occupations in India, it is overwhelmingly done by women, it is often the only formal-sector work available in a village, and it is classified as voluntary service precisely so that it need not be paid as employment.
High in the sense that the posts exist in every village and turnover is real. It is not high in the sense of a growing career - the number of sanctioned anganwadi centres is largely fixed.

admin_review.reason: The honorarium figure is Delhi's, which is at the generous end. No state-by-state range was fetched, and the spread is the single most decision-relevant fact for a student considering this work. Also unresolved: whether an occupation the state deliberately classifies as voluntary service rather than employment should be presented in a salary field at all.

professions.one_liner: Teaches a trade to people who will do it - ITI, apprenticeship and skilling programmes.

deviating_roles.why: Assessment under the National Skills Qualifications Framework is judging whether a candidate meets a written standard, on behalf of a Sector Skill Council. The assessor does not train the people they assess.
Employability training is communication, interviews and workplace behaviour rather than a trade. It is attached to skilling programmes and is a different job entirely.
Trade instruction is demonstration at a bench or a machine, taught by someone who did the job. It is the closest teaching gets to the trade itself.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream, or an ITI trade certificate.
Work in the trade. This is what actually qualifies a vocational trainer and no course substitutes for it.
Craft Instructor Training Scheme (CITS) for ITI posts, or a Sector Skill Council Train-the-Trainer certification for NSQF programmes.
Government or private ITI, a skilling partner under PMKVY, a corporate training centre, or an industry apprenticeship programme.

entrance_exams.note: CITS is the recognised public qualification for ITI instructors; Sector Skill Council certifications govern who may deliver and assess NSQF-aligned training.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Running a private training centre affiliated to a Sector Skill Council, or independent corporate and industrial training. Both depend on holding the certifications that let you certify others.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure, protected by the same thing the trades themselves are protected by: you cannot teach someone to weld through a screen. Placement & Employability Trainer and Assessor (NSQF) carry the exposure - communication training and standards-based assessment are both substantially generatable. ITI Instructor and Workshop Instructor are as safe as the trade they teach.

nuances.statement: Moderate and policy-driven rather than market-driven, which is a real risk worth naming. A large part of this profession is employed through government skilling schemes, so demand moves with scheme funding cycles rather than with the underlying need for trained workers.

Placed in Education rather than Sector 2 with the trades, on the teaching-anything rule. The counterpart decision is that a working electrician stays in Sector 2 - the same subject, split by whether you do the work or teach it.

professions.one_liner: Builds and runs training for people already in jobs - skills, systems, compliance, leadership.

deviating_roles.why: Technical training teaches a specific system or product to people who will use it at work. It requires the underlying domain knowledge and is usually done by someone who moved across from the technical role.
These are performance-led roles - a room of adults who did not choose to be there and must be won over in the first ten minutes.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree.
Several years doing the work you will train. Almost nobody enters corporate training directly from a degree, which makes this a second career rather than a first.
In-house L&D team, a training consultancy, or independent practice.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Independent training consultancy charging per day or per programme. Very common in this profession and the standard second half of the career.

ai_exposure.reason: Substantially exposed on the content side and protected on the delivery side. Compliance Training Specialist and Onboarding Specialist produce standardised material that generates well, and Learning Experience Designer is exposed for the same reason instructional design generally is. What survives is the room: reading whether thirty adults have actually understood something, and being credible to them because you have done the job.

nuances.statement: Six years, and it is not study - it is the domain experience the job requires before anyone will listen to you. This is a SECOND career, entered in the late twenties or thirties, and it should not be presented to a school student as a direct destination.

Promised to this sector from Sector 5. It sits in Education rather than Business because the object of concern is whether a person learns something, and the employer being a company is exactly what DECISIONS.md 2.2 calls a tag.

professions.one_liner: Designs what gets taught and how - syllabi, textbooks, courses, assessments, e-learning.

deviating_roles.why: Education research measures whether teaching worked, using survey and statistical method. It is empirical work and sits close to Sector 3.
E-learning development is authoring-tool and multimedia production work. It is the technical end of the profession and the most directly exposed.
Coordination is timetables, teacher support and academic operations inside a school or institution. It is administration with a curriculum attached.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree; a master's in education, a subject discipline or instructional design helps.
Samples of designed material - a module, an assessment, a course outline. Teaching experience is the commonest way in.
Edtech company, publisher, university teaching and learning centre, NGO, or a corporate L&D team.

entrance_exams.note: None.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance curriculum and content development for publishers, edtech firms and institutions, usually project by project. Common after five or six years.

ai_exposure.reason: The most exposed profession in this sector. Generating a lesson sequence, a set of practice questions or a module outline is close to a canonical use of a language model, and Educational Content Developer, Assessment & Question Designer and E-learning Developer all sit directly in it. What holds is deciding what a specific cohort needs to learn and in what order, defending that against a syllabus committee, and knowing why the previous version failed - which is clarity, and is what Education Researcher and Curriculum Developer do.

nuances.statement: The bottom rung is shrinking hard here. Content development was the standard entry job in Indian edtech and it employed very large numbers of graduates; that intake has visibly contracted. The senior design and research work is intact, but the ladder that produced people for it is not.

professions.one_liner: Organises knowledge so people can find it - libraries, archives, digital collections.

deviating_roles.why: Managing an institutional repository is metadata, standards and systems work. It is the part of librarianship that is closest to data engineering and the part that is growing.
Teaching students how to search, evaluate sources and avoid plagiarism is front-of-room teaching, and it has become the most defensible part of the profession.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree, then B.Lib.I.Sc and usually M.Lib.I.Sc.
UGC NET in Library and Information Science for college and university librarian posts.
University, college, school, public library system, research institute or corporate information centre. Most good posts are government and filled by examination.

entrance_exams.note: UGC NET is the eligibility condition for academic librarian posts, in the same way it is for Assistant Professor.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Freelance cataloguing, records management and knowledge-management consultancy for institutions and companies. A thin market, and it depends on the digital skills rather than the traditional ones.

ai_exposure.reason: Genuinely contested. Cataloguer and Library Assistant work is substantially automatable - metadata generation and classification are pattern tasks - and search itself has been the profession's competition for two decades. What has grown rather than shrunk is Information Literacy Instructor and Digital Repository Manager: when finding text became free, judging and curating it became the job.

nuances.statement: Low, and honestly so. School and college librarian posts in India are frequently unfilled or merged into other duties, and public library systems are thinly funded. The work exists; the sanctioned posts are shrinking.

Placed in Education rather than Sector 17 with heritage. An archivist preserving a collection for its own sake would belong in 17; a librarian exists so that a specific community of readers can learn, which is this sector's object of concern.

professions.one_liner: Helps students choose what to study and what to do next, and understands the routes.

deviating_roles.why: These are commission and target-driven roles representing institutions, which creates a conflict of interest the counselling roles do not have. It is the largest paid segment of the profession and the one a student should understand clearly.
In-school guidance overlaps with pastoral and mental health support, and often involves the first conversation a distressed adolescent has with an adult.
Administering and interpreting aptitude and interest inventories is technical measurement work with a professional standard behind it, done for other counsellors as much as for students.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree; psychology, education or social work is the usual background.
A career counselling certification, or a master's in psychology or education. Nothing is legally required.
School counselling cell, private practice, an edtech or admissions company, or a college placement office.

entrance_exams.note: No public entrance and no statutory qualification. This is one of the least regulated advisory roles a family will ever pay for.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Independent counselling practice charging per student or per assessment, and school retainers. Common, and it is where the profession's better practitioners end up.

ai_exposure.reason: High retrievable-knowledge content and it shows: the factual half of this job - which exam, which cutoff, which college, which deadline - is exactly what a well-built system answers better than a person. Admissions Counsellor and Study Abroad Consultant are directly exposed on that. What survives is the part this dataset exists to support rather than replace: knowing a specific sixteen-year-old, and what their family can afford, fear and accept.

nuances.statement: Null, and this is a consumer-protection gap worth stating on the record. Anyone in India may charge a family for career advice with no qualification, no register and no complaints route, and a large part of the paid market is commission-based representation of colleges rather than advice.

Placed here rather than in Sector 13 with psychology because the object of concern is an educational and occupational decision, not wellbeing. The boundary is real: a school guidance counsellor doing clinical work needs RCI registration, and this profession does not.

professions.one_liner: Assesses and treats mental illness - the only psychology role India licenses.

deviating_roles.why: Assessment work is standardised test administration, scoring and report writing. It is measurement rather than therapy, and much of it is done for a referring doctor or a court rather than for the person in the chair.

Forensic work serves a legal question rather than a patient, is adversarial, and ends in cross-examination. RCI registration is what makes the expert evidence admissible under Section 45 of the Indian Evidence Act.
Community practice is outreach in low-resource settings - district hospitals, camps and homes - with far less diagnostic apparatus and far more social context.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream. Psychology is available in arts, commerce and science streams and is not required at school.
BA or BSc Psychology (3-4 years).
MA or MSc in Psychology or Clinical Psychology (2 years).
M.Phil in Clinical Psychology (2 years) at an RCI-recognised institution, including supervised clinical training. THIS is the step that makes practice lawful, and places are very few.
Enrolment on the Central Rehabilitation Register. Mandatory - practising without it is an offence under Section 13 of the RCI Act.

entrance_exams.note: The M.Phil entrance is the real gate. It is institution-specific rather than national, which is why no single figure exists for how hard it is - and that opacity is itself a problem for a student planning this route.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Private practice, which is the normal destination. RCI registration is what makes it lawful and what lets a practitioner charge clinical rates rather than counselling rates.

ai_exposure.reason: Very low exposure once legal accountability is applied, and the reason is the strongest in the model: a registered human must assess, decide and carry liability, and Section 13(2) of the RCI Act makes that a legal requirement rather than a convention. Psycho-diagnostician work is the most exposed - test scoring and report drafting are substantially automatable - but the signature and the responsibility cannot move.

nuances.statement: Tier A and criminally enforced. Section 13(2) of the RCI Act 1992 bars an unregistered person from practising as a clinical psychologist anywhere in India or giving expert evidence; Section 13(3) makes contravention punishable with up to a year's imprisonment. The Mental Healthcare Act 2017 defines a clinical psychologist by reference to the same RCI recognition.

'after_any_degree' is technically true - the master's admission is what matters - but psychology master's programmes in practice want a psychology bachelor's, so a commerce or engineering graduate is usually restarting rather than switching. Read this as the door being open and narrow, not open and wide.

Nine years from class 12, and the bottleneck is the last two. The M.Phil in Clinical Psychology is the only route to lawful practice and India runs very few recognised places, so a large number of psychology postgraduates never reach it and work unregistered as counsellors instead.

High and severely undersupplied - India has a very small number of registered clinical psychologists for its population. The shortage does not translate into easy entry, because the constraint is M.Phil seats rather than demand.

professions.one_liner: Talks people through difficulty - the mental health work India does not regulate at all.

deviating_roles.why: Genetic counselling explains inheritance risk and test results to a family making a reproductive or treatment decision. It requires genetics rather than psychology training and is the only role here with a scientific knowledge base as its core.

Addiction work involves relapse, deception and confrontation, often in residential settings, and a large share of practitioners are themselves in recovery. It is the least gentle work in this profession.
Helpline work is single anonymous contacts, often in crisis, with no follow-up and no history. The skill is stabilising a stranger in twenty minutes.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Usually a BA or BSc in Psychology, then an MA or MSc. Nothing is legally required, which is the defining fact about this profession.
A counselling or psychotherapy diploma and supervised practice hours. Reputable, entirely voluntary, and not verifiable by a client.
School counselling cell, NGO, helpline, de-addiction centre, corporate wellbeing programme, or private practice.

entrance_exams.note: No statutory qualification exists. University admission is a normal one and confers no right to practise, because no such right is regulated.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Private practice, seen either online or from a room, charging per session. Entry requires nothing but a client, which is both why the profession is accessible and why it is unsafe.

ai_exposure.reason: Clarity-heavy, and the band was raised to medium on the second pass because a low band contradicted this very paragraph. A counselling conversation IS output a model can produce, which is what skill_digital measures, and pretending otherwise understated the one profession here where AI competes with the SERVICE rather than the admin around it. This is the profession where AI chat products compete most directly with the service itself rather than with the work around it. Helpline Counsellor and Workplace Wellbeing Counsellor face that first, since both are single-contact and text-mediated. Marriage & Family Counsellor and Addiction & De-addiction Counsellor are protected by the work being relational and confrontational over months.

nuances.statement: Null, and it is the most important thing on this record. The titles 'counsellor' and 'psychotherapist' carry NO statutory register in India - the RCI Act does not list a general counsellor among rehabilitation professionals. Anyone may use the title and charge for therapy. Association membership is not registration, and a client cannot tell the difference from a job title.

Deliberately separated from Clinical Psychologist rather than merged, despite overlapping work. The two share an object of concern and much of a skill set, which would normally trigger the merge test in DECISIONS.md 8.95 - but one is Tier A with criminal enforcement and a nine-year runway, and the other has no gate at all. Merging them would hide exactly the distinction a student and a client most need.

Sits below Clinical Psychologist for the same reason it is easier to enter: no registration means no protected scope, so rates are set by an open market with no floor. Practitioners who also hold an RCI registration charge clinical rates; those who do not, compete on price.

professions.one_liner: Works with people the system is failing - families, children, patients, the displaced.

deviating_roles.why: Hospital-based social work sits inside a clinical team - discharge planning, family counselling and welfare linkage. Psychiatric social work has an RCI-recognised M.Phil route of its own, which puts part of this role under the same statute as clinical psychology.
Relief work is physically hard field deployment at short notice into unsafe places. It is the least desk-bound social work there is.
These are statutory posts with legal reporting duties to a court or a Child Welfare Committee. The social worker carries authority as well as care, which changes the relationship entirely.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
BSW, or any bachelor's degree followed by an MSW. The MSW is what the field actually recruits on.
Supervised fieldwork placements, which are built into the MSW and are where employability is decided.
NGO, hospital, government department, corporate CSR team, or a statutory post such as Probation Officer.

public_routes: TISS and central university MSW admissions
State recruitment for Probation and Child Welfare Officer posts
entrance_exams.note: MSW admission is the practical gate. TISS and a handful of central universities are the sought-after routes; state universities admit far more people with much less competition.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Independent consultancy to NGOs and funders on programme design, safeguarding and evaluation, usually after ten years in the field.

ai_exposure.reason: Low exposure. The work is being physically present with people in difficulty, in homes, hospitals, shelters and courts, and holding a case over months. Case Worker documentation and reporting is the exposed part and it is real - social workers spend a great deal of time on records - but automating the paperwork frees the job rather than removing it.

nuances.statement: Psychiatric social work has an RCI-recognised M.Phil route and therefore falls under the same Act as clinical psychology, unlike the rest of this profession. A student intending hospital mental health work should read the Clinical Psychologist record alongside this one.

Null, and deliberately so. MSW admission is the practical gate and it now runs largely through CUET PG - but pointing this record at CUET UG would repeat the mistake corrected in Sector 3, telling a would-be social worker that the hard part is getting into a bachelor's degree. It is not. The MSW admission is in pending_gates.

Split by employer rather than by ability. A statutory government post - Probation Officer, Child Welfare Officer - carries a pay scale and a pension; the NGO sector pays modestly and on project funding cycles; corporate CSR pays best and employs fewest. The same MSW leads to all three.

Moderate, and it depends on funding rather than need. The need is enormous and constant; the number of funded posts moves with government scheme budgets and CSR compliance, which is a different signal entirely.

professions.one_liner: Designs and runs programmes meant to change something - poverty, health, education, rights.

deviating_roles.why: Raising money is proposal writing, donor relationships and reporting against commitments. It is the commercial function of the development sector and it pays best, precisely because everything else depends on it.
Field officers live in the block or district they work in and do the actual mobilisation. It is the entry rung, it is where the sector's knowledge comes from, and it is paid least.

Advocacy is public and adversarial - pressing government or business to change policy. It sits close to the Public Policy Professional in Sector 7 and differs by being outside the state rather than inside it.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream.
Any bachelor's degree. MSW, development studies, rural management (IRMA), public policy and economics are all common routes in.
A fellowship or field stint - Gandhi Fellowship, Prime Minister's Rural Development Fellows, SBI Youth for India and similar. This is how most people actually enter.
NGO, foundation, multilateral agency, government programme unit, or a corporate CSR team.

private_entrances: Development fellowships (Gandhi Fellowship, PMRDF and others)
entrance_exams.note: There is no gate specific to this profession. CAT is listed because a rural-management or MBA route into development is common and is one of the better-paid ways in.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Independent consultancy to NGOs, funders and government programmes - programme design, evaluation and proposal writing. Common after eight to ten years and generally better paid than the salaried version.

ai_exposure.reason: Moderately exposed on the paperwork and protected on the ground. Programme Documentation Officer and much of Fundraising & Grants Officer work - proposals, donor reports, log frames - is templated writing that generates well, and that is a large share of the sector's desk time. Field Officer and Advocacy & Campaigns Officer are protected by needing to be in a village or a room with people who can say no.

nuances.statement: Moderate and structurally unstable. Employment here follows grant cycles, CSR compliance and government scheme budgets rather than the underlying problem, so posts appear and vanish on two-to-three-year project timelines. That instability is the profession's defining employment characteristic and is invisible in a salary range.

Pathway is 'any' because this is one of the few Indian professions with a genuine international ladder that does not require emigration - multilateral agencies, international NGOs and global foundations recruit in India for regional roles.

professions.one_liner: Measures whether a social programme actually worked, and says so when it did not.

deviating_roles.why: Running a field study means recruiting and managing dozens of enumerators across districts and protecting data quality when nobody is watching. It is operations management with a research standard attached.
Social audit is reading government scheme records aloud to the village the scheme was meant to serve. It is a public accountability ritual and it is sometimes dangerous.

path_to_entry.requirement: Any stream. Mathematics helps substantially and is not required.
Economics, statistics, development studies, public policy or social sciences. The quantitative half of this job is what makes it distinct.
Research associate at a research organisation, an evaluation firm or an NGO's M&E unit. This is a recognised entry job with a defined skill test.
Impact evaluation, survey methods or programme MIS. The first transfers to economics research and academia.

public_routes: Master's in economics and public policy admissions
entrance_exams.note: No profession-specific gate. Entry is on demonstrable statistical and field-research skill.

economics.basis: mid_career is 5-8 years of EMPLOYMENT after entering the field, EMPLOYED only. Independent practice and business ownership are excluded - that income is entrepreneurship, and self_employment carries it separately.

self_employment.route: Independent evaluation consultancy, which is a real market - funders increasingly require third-party evaluation, and an evaluator's independence is the product.

ai_exposure.reason: The most exposed profession in this sector. MIS & Reporting Analyst and Data Analyst (Development) do work that is directly substitutable - cleaning, tabulating and charting survey data - and much of routine M&E reporting is already automated in dashboards. What survives is study design and the willingness to report a null result: deciding what would count as evidence that a programme failed, and saying so to the people who funded it.

nuances.statement: Kept separate from Development & Programme Professional rather than folded in as job roles. They share an object of concern but not a skill set - this is quantitative research method, survey design and statistics, and the merge test in DECISIONS.md 8.95 turns on the skill set being separate.

Tagged EXT-RND as well as EXT-DEV. The boundary with Sector 3 is the one DECISIONS.md 2 draws by METHOD rather than discipline: this is empirical, quantitative work, and it sits here only because its object of concern is whether an intervention helped rather than what is true in general.

professions.one_liner: Organises people in a village or neighbourhood to claim services and run things themselves.

deviating_roles.why: Village level entrepreneurs run a service - a common service centre, a banking correspondent point, an agri-input shop - on commission rather than salary. It is a small business wearing a development job's clothes.

Coordination roles sit between the field and the district office - reporting, verification and scheme paperwork. They are the first step off the field and the only visible promotion in this profession.

path_to_entry.requirement: Class 10 or 12. Many roles specify residence in the block or village as a condition.
